Second, do the temporal edits cover long-range dependencies found in real video understanding, or mostly local order changes? Third, can this structured counterfactual-negative recipe transfer to audio, speech, or interleaved multimodal sequence modeling?76:T618,The design is careful and controlled. The dataset consists of 237 step-numbered solutions to 79 Humanity’s Last Exam physics questions, generated by three frontier models, with no synthetic error insertion. Each trace is labeled for two targets: final-answer correctness and the location of the first false step. The reference standard combines physicist annotations, an independent LLM debate, and source-masked adjudication, which is a sensible way to reduce single-annotator bias on difficult technical derivations.

The key experimental device is an information ladder that varies only the epistemic status of the answer shown to the monitor: blind, unverified answer, certified answer, and answer revealed only after a blind commitment. There is also a reconsideration control and a stepwise online condition. This lets the authors separate error detection from first-error localization, and further split traces into wrong-answer cases versus correct-answer-but-flawed cases. That decomposition is the core contribution. It turns a vague question about “monitoring reasoning” into a cleaner measurement of whether the monitor is validating the argument or merely using the answer as a shortcut.

Another good choice is that the same trace is evaluated under different monitoring conditions. The paper avoids across-question correctness prediction, where models can exploit question difficulty or benchmark priors. Here the object being judged is fixed, so differences are much more plausibly due to answer access rather than prompt-level confounds.77:T64a,The dataset is modest in size but strong in curation. There are 237 traces from 79 HLE physics questions, and the generating models achieve about 65% final-answer correctness on this filtered subset, so the benchmark contains both positive and negative cases. The most important subset is the 24 critical traces where the final answer is correct but the reasoning contains a real error. Those are the cases that remove the easy shortcut of checking whether the conclusion is wrong.

Eight LLM monitors are evaluated. The headline result in the abstract is that certification of the answer raises mean detection performance, but the gain comes mainly from traces with incorrect final answers. On the critical traces, answer access provides little benefit, and first-error localization barely improves. That is the central empirical point: when the answer is wrong, monitors behave more like outcome checkers; when the answer is right but the process is flawed, their actual argument-verification ability is much weaker.

A useful background number from the paper is that 65% of traces end with the correct answer, yet some of those traces are still invalid. The authors explicitly connect this to the structure of reward hacking: acceptable output does not imply acceptable process. If monitoring relies on answer visibility, these cases will be systematically missed.

The most informative comparisons are not between monitor models, but between conditions: blind vs unverified vs certified vs commit-then-reveal. Those deltas support the paper’s main claim that answer access changes what is being measured.78:T74e,The benchmark, VoiceLongMemEval, is built around a strict invariant: every item must be solvable from paralinguistic metadata and unsolvable from text alone. To enforce that, each user turn is annotated with five layers: one of 12 everyday emotion labels, a prosody tuple covering rate, pitch, loudness, pauses, and emphasized words, one of five voice-event types, pragmatic flags such as sarcasm and uncertainty, and a free-text delivery description. A good design choice is that the free-text description is constrained to acoustic facts only. Interpretive emotion words are banned, so the task does not collapse into keyword matching.

Construction proceeds through annotation, evidence authoring and hardening, question generation, and speech synthesis. A small number of evidence sessions are embedded into roughly 100k-token conversation histories together with topic-screened filler sessions and emotive but answer-free distractors. Needle positions are stratified over early, middle, and late parts of the history, and multi-evidence arcs are distributed across sessions. This makes the benchmark closer to long-horizon retrieval under realistic clutter rather than a short-context classification task.

The most important engineering contribution is the three-stage adversarial gate against lexical leakage. G1 requires the blind transcript-only render to be unsolvable. G2 checks that the descriptive render with paralinguistic metadata is solvable. G3 applies static checks for interpretive terms, stock phrases, and valence-presupposing wording. The authors iterate with a 7B judge-adversary and then gate with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-AWQ, requiring two consecutive clean runs on a frozen file. That is a sensible response to the main failure mode of this benchmark family: if the text itself leaks the answer, the task no longer measures paralinguistic memory.79:T6cb,The benchmark contains 523 questions in total, with a 202-item adversarially gated core, built from 326 paralinguistically annotated evidence sessions embedded in about 100k-token histories. The taxonomy covers six task types: affect recall, affective preference, affect update, cross-session affect, temporal-affective reasoning, and prosody-disambiguated interpretation, plus abstention variants.

Eight models are evaluated, including three proprietary and five open-weight systems. The main result is a consistent affect gap: access to paralinguistic information improves performance by +0.09 to +0.38 across all systems, with p < 0.001. Component ablations show that explicit emotion tags are the strongest signal. The paper also argues that chain-of-thought cannot compensate for missing paralinguistic context. In controlled counterfactual analysis, the net gain attributable strictly to metadata content is about +0.067.

The benchmark-construction diagnostics are also useful. A 72B blind adversary still solved 8 items, or 7.5%, after earlier 7B gating. The authors categorize leakage into five mechanisms: pragmatic-prior leakage, outcome tells, gold-matches-prior, default-recovery priors, and A/B gifts. Later batches reportedly removed authoring-time leaks. That part is benchmark engineering, but it is informative because it exposes common ways long-context evaluations accidentally become text-solvable.

From a pretraining perspective, the most relevant findings are not leaderboard differences. The important takeaways are that transcript-only representations systematically lose memory-relevant information, and that structured paralinguistic metadata is a stronger and more reliable signal than extra reasoning tokens.7a:T7cb,There are three main design choices. First, the dataset is built from active but less canonical scientific literature rather than textbook equations. The final benchmark contains 118 problems, 291 candidate laws, 381 papers, and about 8M real data points across six disciplines. It also includes both single-group and multi-group settings. In the multi-group case, models must infer a shared functional form while allowing some parameters to vary across groups, which is closer to real scientific modeling than fitting one global curve.

Second, evaluation is split into two complementary settings. In SciLaws-Real, the model receives fixed real observations and must propose a closed-form law. Published formulas are treated as references, not mandatory targets. Proposed laws are judged along two separate axes: held-out predictive fit and source-grounded scientific validity. This is an important distinction. A formula can fit well numerically and still be scientifically wrong if it violates domain constraints, behaves badly in the relevant regime, or introduces unsupported mechanisms.

Third, SciLaws-Parallel converts the same scientific problem into an active experimental environment. The hidden law is not the published one; it is a newly synthesized structural variant derived from the published form, with coefficients and residual noise calibrated to the corresponding real records. Models start without observations, choose measurements under a fixed budget, and try to recover the hidden law. This setup preserves scientific context while making it possible to test novel-structure recovery rather than literature recall.

Operationally, the authors evaluate nine frontier LLMs under a unified ReAct-style agent framework, with a Python sandbox and, for the parallel setting, a fixed-budget experimentation interface. Each trial allows up to 30 interaction turns, so the benchmark measures multi-step reasoning and tool-mediated exploration rather than one-shot text generation.7b:T5e1,The main empirical findings are threefold. First, models struggle to balance predictive accuracy and scientific validity. The paper gives a nuclear-physics example where the best-fitting formula introduces a nonexistent resonance peak, so it fails the validity check despite good numerical fit. This shows why held-out error alone is not enough.

Second, models are much better at reproducing known laws than at discovering new structure. A cold-recall audit indicates that SciLaws-Bench is less memorized than textbook-style benchmarks. Under weaker recall, models do explore beyond published formulas more often, but successful recovery of genuinely novel structure remains rare. Exploration is present; robust structural induction is not.

Third, models can generate stronger candidates than they can reliably select. Best-of-N search consistently exposes better formulas, but self-selection captures only a small fraction of that gain. This is an important result because it shifts part of the bottleneck from proposal generation to ranking, verification, and candidate selection.

In terms of scale, the benchmark covers 118 problems, 291 candidate laws, 381 papers, and roughly 8M real data points, and evaluates nine frontier models including GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro. The full paper contains the detailed tables, but the headline conclusion is clear: current LLMs show signs of scientific-law discovery ability, yet the capability is still far from reliable.7c:T403,Start with the introduction and Figure 1 to understand why the benchmark is split into SciLaws-Real and SciLaws-Parallel. Then read the benchmark construction section carefully: the paper-selection criteria, the cold-recall audit, and the role of single-group versus multi-group tasks are all central. After that, focus on the evaluation protocol, especially how predictive fit is separated from scientific validity and how the hidden-law synthesis in the parallel world avoids collapsing into a purely synthetic toy setup.

In the results, three analyses deserve priority: cases where fit and validity disagree, the relationship between recall and novel-structure recovery, and the gap between best-of-N generation and model self-selection. Those sections are enough for a useful skim in about 35 to 50 minutes. If reading more deeply, pay attention to how stable the validity rubric is, whether the synthesized structural variants introduce distribution shift, and how much the fixed interaction budget affects model ranking.7d:T8e8,方法上，这篇文章做得比较扎实，重点不在模型创新，而在协议设计和误差定位。

第一，作者在两个域上统一了评测协议。数学部分使用 MathNet-Retrieve：500 个 query，对 117,088 条完整语料全库排序，不做 shortlist。每个 query 都有唯一 gold source problem，同时 benchmark 还人为放入一个 lexical 相近但结构不同的 near-miss。作者同时报告 strict Hit@k（只认 gold）和 lenient Hit@k（gold 或 near-miss 都算），这个差值正好用来量化“模型是不是被表面相似项吸走了”。

第二，trajectory 部分没有沿用原 benchmark 的 pooled relevance，而是把 336 条 ALFWorld 轨迹全部按 task type 重新穷举标注，并进一步定义两层 disguise：定义(i)要求同 task type 但 target object 不同；定义(ii)再额外要求 receptacle 也不同，尽量去掉最容易驱动 lexical similarity 的 token。这里的设计很关键，因为它把“程序相同”与“对象词相同”拆开了。

第三，作者专门研究 lexical control 的符号翻转。他们引入一个便宜的 lexical reranker，观察它在两个域里的效果方向：在数学里它会伤害结构检索，因为它把 near-miss 顶上去；在轨迹里它反而能提升结果，因为 benchmark 构造仍保留了某些表面线索。随后又做 token-class ablation，去定位究竟是哪些 token 类别在驱动这个现象。

第四，作者分析了 LLM reranking 的 judge dependence。不是只看“加了 reranker 后有没有提升”，而是换三个独立训练的 judge，看恢复方向是否稳定、效应量是否可迁移。结论是方向大体一致，但幅度、tier profile、甚至哪个 judge 更强，都会随域和 query style 改变。这说明 reranker/judge 的结论可移植性很差。

第五，文章还做了 contamination probe 和 downstream null analysis。前者检查 reranking 增益是否集中在知名竞赛题上；后者在一个刻意构造的坏检索条件下比较 oracle retrieval 与 adversarial retrieval，发现下游几乎无差异，并进一步把原因定位到答案截断与评测解析问题，而不是 retrieval 真没作用。这个部分虽然偏评测卫生，但很有现实意义。7e:T873,最关键的结果在数学检索。重 disguise 条件下，两个 production embedders 的 strict Hit@1 都是 0.0%，bootstrap 95% CI 也是 [0.0, 0.0]。但正确答案通常并没有消失，而是“在 top-10 里几乎总能找到”。这说明问题不是召回不到，而是排序头部被 lexical near-miss 占据。作者进一步统计 miss 的构成：在 95.2% 到 99.8% 的 miss 中，排在正确答案前面的候选在词面上比 gold 更接近 query。这基本把失败机制钉死在 surface-form bias 上。

轨迹检索的结果更微妙。只要 gold 定义排除了 query 中的 literal object 和 receptacle token，embedding retrieval 就会掉到 chance 以下。这个现象比“性能下降”更强，因为它说明模型不仅没抓住结构，反而系统性偏向错误的表面匹配项。

lexical reranker 的实验是全文最有信息量的对照之一：同一个 lexical control，在数学上伤害 retrieval，在 trajectory 上提升 retrieval。作者通过 token-class ablation 说明，这不是偶然噪声，而是 benchmark 中哪些 token 被保留、哪些被 disguise 的结果。

LLM reranking 部分，作者发现三个 judge 在“是否有恢复趋势”上方向一致，但效应量并不稳定；其中一个 judge 在同一域内跨 query style 时，增益会下降超过三分之一。也就是说，judge 排名本身都不稳。

污染分析里，reranking 的收益更多集中在知名竞赛题；在 6 个 judge-by-candidate cell 中，只有 1 个在 bootstrap 下能自信拒绝零效应，其余更多是方向一致但统计强度不足。这个表述比较克制，没有把 contamination 说得过头。

下游实验里，作者构造了 oracle retrieval 与 adversarial retrieval 的配对比较，结果几乎无差异。进一步做 complete-answers-only 分析后，发现原先 headline 的 69.5% zero-shot accuracy 很大程度上只是 truncation proxy，导致 retrieval 实际可发挥的 headroom 接近于零。另一个很实用的结果是，他们记录了 8 个 evaluation-integrity incident，其中多数与 silent truncation 被误解析为有效输出有关。7f:T813,The contribution is in protocol design and failure localization, not in proposing a new retriever.

First, the authors enforce a shared evaluation protocol across two domains. In mathematics, they use 500 queries from MathNet-Retrieve against the full 117,088-item MathNet corpus, with no shortlist. Each query has exactly one gold source problem, plus a planted lexical near-miss that is structurally different. They report both strict Hit@k, which counts only the gold, and lenient Hit@k, which also counts the near-miss. The gap between the two is a direct measure of surface-form attraction.

Second, for ALFWorld trajectories they do not rely on pooled relevance from the source benchmark. Instead, they exhaustively label all 336 corpus items by task type and define two disguise regimes: same task type but different target object, and then same task type with both object and receptacle changed. This is important because it separates procedural similarity from literal token overlap.

Third, they study a lexical-control sign flip. A simple lexical reranker is applied in both domains. In math it hurts structural retrieval by promoting the planted near-miss; in trajectories it helps because the benchmark still preserves some surface cues. Token-class ablations are then used to identify which token categories drive the effect.

Fourth, they analyze judge dependence for LLM reranking. Instead of reporting a single reranking gain, they compare three independently trained judges and ask whether the recovery direction, effect size, and judge ranking are stable across domains and query styles. The answer is largely no for effect size portability.

Fifth, they add a contamination probe and a downstream null analysis. The contamination probe checks whether reranking gains concentrate on well-known competition problems. The downstream analysis compares oracle and adversarial retrieval under a deliberately bad retrieval condition and then traces the null result to truncation and evaluation artifacts rather than to retrieval being inherently useless.80:T7f3,The strongest result is in mathematics. Under the heaviest disguise tier, strict Hit@1 is 0.0% for both production embedders, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of [0.0, 0.0]. But the gold item is usually still retrievable: it is almost always somewhere in the top 10. So the failure is not recall collapse; it is head-of-list ranking being captured by lexical near-misses. The mechanism is quantified directly: in 95.2% to 99.8% of misses, the item ranked above the gold is more lexically similar to the query than the correct answer.

The trajectory results are subtler but arguably more revealing. Once the gold definition excludes the literal object and receptacle tokens from the query, embedding retrieval falls below chance. That is stronger than a simple degradation result: it indicates systematic attraction toward the wrong surface match.

The lexical reranker experiment is one of the most informative controls in the paper. The same lexical signal damages retrieval in mathematics and improves it in trajectories. Token-class ablations support the claim that this is driven by benchmark construction, not by noise.

For LLM reranking, the recovery direction replicates across three judges, but the effect size does not transport cleanly. One judge loses more than a third of its gains across query styles within the same domain. So even judge ranking is unstable.

In the contamination probe, reranking gains are concentrated on well-known competitions. Out of six judge-by-candidate cells, only one is confidently non-null under bootstrap resampling, while the others are directionally consistent but weaker statistically.

In the downstream study, oracle and adversarial retrieval are effectively indistinguishable. A complete-answers-only analysis then shows that the headline 69.5% zero-shot accuracy is largely a truncation proxy, leaving almost no effective headroom for retrieval to matter. The paper also documents eight evaluation-integrity incidents, most involving silent truncation parsed as valid output.81:T4cf,ExBind is built around a representation-independent latent binding space and deterministic compilation/evaluation:
1) Sample a latent binding instance containing entities, relations, hierarchy, attributes, ordered roles (e.g., directed edge endpoints), and a unique canonical target.
2) Compile the same latent instance into heterogeneous executable surfaces (SVG, DOM, canvas, tree, graph, table), each with its own surface-specific executable identifiers.
3) The model outputs only the reference required by the environment. The evaluator maps the prediction back into the latent space deterministically, then reports:
- validity (is the output a valid candidate under the declared vocabulary/format?)
- exact binding correctness (does it match the gold target?)
- which structural constraints are violated; for families with an ordered constraint decomposition, a concise first-violation diagnosis.
4) The benchmark explicitly distinguishes outcome stability from diagnostic-type stability via candidate-order perturbations.
The dataset is intentionally small to preserve identifiability: unique gold targets, deterministic mappings, structural-oracle recovery, and shortcut checks are prioritized over population-scale ranking.82:T4b2,Vision-Free Adaptation (VFA) reframes fine-tuning as a task vector and composes task vectors over a shared backbone.
- Let the base text LLM be θ_base. Fine-tune θ_base on multilingual text D_multi to obtain θ_FT. Define the multilingual task vector as Δ_multi = θ_FT − θ_base.
- Given an existing MLLM with backbone parameters θ_MLLM (already vision-aligned), VFA avoids updating θ_MLLM with text-only gradients. Instead it merges the multilingual delta into the MLLM: θ_merged = θ_MLLM + α·Δ_multi, where α controls the trade-off between multilingual gains and preserving multimodal behavior.
- Vision encoder and projection modules are frozen to prevent drifting of cross-modal mapping without visual supervision.
- The paper discusses multiple merging operators (explicitly including weight averaging / linear interpolation) to navigate the stability–plasticity trade-off.

Rationale: direct text-only tuning on θ_MLLM perturbs shared backbone representations that also support vision grounding; learning Δ_multi in the θ_base coordinate system and injecting it as a controlled increment reduces destructive interference and enables reuse across multiple MLLMs sharing θ_base.83:T5df,The paper starts from a tightly controlled comparison: two 32-layer ViTs trained from scratch under identical settings, differing only in the attention operator—full attention versus Qwen-style chunk-window attention. Inspecting per-head attention maps, the authors observe that full-attention heads tend to specialize into semantic roles, with some focusing more on foreground objects and others on background regions. Chunk-window attention shows much weaker specialization and more uniform grid-like patterns. This phenomenon is named Semantic Head Specialization (SHS).

To quantify it, the paper introduces SHS-Index, an AUROC-based metric that measures how well a head separates foreground from background tokens. The metric is then evaluated on 16 open-source visual encoders and VLMs, where it cleanly separates full-attention and chunk-window families. The authors also show that changing only the LLM backbone size in Qwen2.5-VL barely changes SHS-Index, suggesting that the signal is driven by ViT attention design rather than language model scale.

The paper then analyzes three structural factors that affect SHS: window interaction, token serialization, and local softmax allocation. Based on these findings, it proposes Ariadne Attention, which combines sliding windows, per-head sink bias, and row-column alternating serialization. The design logic is diagnostic-driven: identify what full attention preserves internally, then build a cheaper hybrid that retains more of that property.84:T5da,VLAct is best understood as a recipe, not a new backbone family. The first component is preserving the VLM prior. The model uses shallow-layer protection to reduce destructive drift in early representations, and caption-data mixing to keep generic semantic anchors alive during robot continued pre-training. This is a deliberate choice: robot trajectories provide action supervision but poor coverage of open-world semantics, so relying on them alone would adapt faster but forget more. The second component is multi-head continuous action co-supervision. During continued pre-training, the same backbone is trained against multiple continuous action heads rather than a single head. The point is not to deploy all heads later, but to prevent the backbone from collapsing onto one head’s output geometry and to encourage head-agnostic action representations. The third component is a partially unified cross-embodiment action layout. Instead of fully separate robot-specific action spaces or an overly rigid global unification, the method aligns semantically comparable action dimensions where possible and uses a wrap-aware loss for periodic joints so angular variables are trained with the correct topology. This middle ground matters because embodiments are related but not identical. A notable design choice throughout the paper is that these mechanisms are used to shape the backbone during continued pre-training; downstream users can still attach whatever action head fits their own setup.85:T4db,The evaluation spans simulation benchmarks, real-world robot settings, and unseen-embodiment transfer. Main numbers reported in the paper include 82.6% on LIBERO-Plus, 54.8% on VLA-Arena, and 92.5% on RoboTwin 2.0. On RoboDojo, VLAct reaches a score of 10.66 with a 7.60% success rate, ranking sixth by success and outperforming all explicitly designated WAM models according to the paper. A particularly strong data-efficiency result is that using only 20% of RoboCasa-GR1 data still surpasses the full-data GR00T-N1.6 baseline. The training setup is also intentionally modest: open-source data only and a 16-GPU run. The most important experimental control is that, across comparisons, only the VLM backbone weights differ; the action head, its fresh initialization, downstream data, optimizer, and fine-tuning budget are held fixed. That makes the attribution to continued-pretrained representations much cleaner. The ablations support the proposed failure-mode analysis: removing shallow-layer protection or caption mixing hurts prior preservation; removing multi-head co-supervision reduces transfer robustness; removing the partially unified action layout and wrap-aware loss weakens cross-embodiment sharing and periodic-joint modeling.86:T51c,SCEval keeps the question, answer space, gold label, and modality channels fixed, and perturbs only the internal structure of one or more modalities. Text corruption means deletion or shuffling rather than removing the text channel. Visual corruption means noise, blur, or occlusion rather than replacing the image/video. Audio corruption means muting, distortion, or segment removal rather than dropping the audio stream. The benchmark uses 14 curated operators: four for text, seven for vision, and three for audio. It evaluates single-, dual-, and tri-modal corruption settings. For stochastic operators, the protocol averages over up to three random variants and also records the worst-variant gap, which is a useful way to expose seed-level fragility without making the main metric depend on one unlucky sample. The dataset is built from 300 candidates sampled from Social-IQ, OmniBench, and VALOR, then filtered by a third-party team down to 273 human-verified tri-modal examples. The filtering criteria are important: the clean item must be valid, the answer must be tri-modally supportable, and the corrupted inputs must remain interpretable to humans. Because the design is sample-paired, clean-versus-corrupted comparisons are made on the same underlying example rather than across shifted subsets.87:T433,The main results are behavioral diagnostics. First, structural corruption consistently reduces clean all-modality accuracy, showing that many apparent omni-modal gains are fragile to internal evidence damage. Second, text-vision joint corruption emerges as the most stable shared fault line, suggesting that this interaction is especially brittle across models. Third, degradation is non-additive and model-dependent: the effect of dual- or tri-modal corruption is not a simple sum of single-modality drops, which implies that different models rely on different evidence pathways. The most striking empirical pattern is that under fixed heavy visual noise, 14 of 15 models perform worse with mildly corrupted text (t30) than with heavily corrupted text (t70). The paper is careful not to over-interpret this, but the result strongly suggests that partially damaged text can be more misleading than obviously broken text. In terms of scale, the benchmark contains 273 human-verified base examples, each expanded into clean, single-, dual-, and tri-modal corruption conditions.88:T568,The authors first run controlled ablations on a compact 13M-example dataset, then scale the resulting recipe to Pixel Linguist II trained on 280M examples. The method has four main components. First, it uses a native-resolution ViT-style encoder, following the NaViT direction, so inputs can have variable resolutions and aspect ratios. The key observation is that high-resolution document pretraining is not always necessary if the model sees suitable spatial proxies: variable natural-image resolutions and variable rendered font sizes. Second, the model uses layout-aware visual augmentation. Text is rendered on the fly with diverse fonts, backgrounds, spatial layouts, and perturbations, reducing the chance that the encoder solves the task through font or canvas artifacts. Third, training combines natural image-text pairs and rendered text-text pairs under a single contrastive objective. Natural images are not merely auxiliary data; they provide grounding and prevent a text-only collapse in the visual domain. Fourth, multilingual learning uses a two-stage curriculum: large-scale unsupervised multilingual visual-text pretraining followed by semantic mid-training for cross-lingual alignment. This differs from prior fixed-resolution, rendered-text-only, single-stage recipes by treating resolution, layout, grounding, and multilinguality as coupled pretraining variables.89:T4a2,The experimental evidence is organized around four research questions. In the 13M-example ablation setting, variable natural-image resolutions and variable rendered font sizes improve transfer to resolution-sensitive document retrieval, supporting the spatial-proxy hypothesis. Removing natural image-text pairs severely degrades dense document retrieval, showing that even text-centric visual tasks benefit from real-world multimodal grounding. Fixed fonts and plain canvases lead to pixel-level shortcuts and near-collapse on document retrieval. For multilingual text, the best setup is a two-stage pipeline: unsupervised multilingual visual-text pretraining followed by semantic mid-training. At scale, Pixel Linguist II is trained on 280M examples and is evaluated on English, cross-lingual, and multilingual Visual STS, ViDoRe visual document retrieval, and as a vision encoder inside multimodal LLMs. The model also remains robust when up to 80% of visual tokens are compressed, which matters for document retrieval and serving cost. The provided text does not include the full numeric tables, so the most reliable signal is the structure of the ablations and their failure cases.8a:T816,The method has two stages. First is AHAF, Adversarial Hallucination Attribute Flipping. Instead of using adversarial perturbations for standard classification attacks, the paper uses PGD to flip the model’s object-existence judgment on the same image, for example from present to absent or vice versa. This produces paired images that are semantically almost identical, with differences concentrated around the visual cues that move the model across a hallucination boundary. That is the key distinction from ordinary contrastive fine-tuning with random negatives: random negatives change too many factors at once, such as scene, object identity, and background, so the model can still solve the task through coarse spatial shortcuts.

Second is ACFT, Adversarial Contrastive Fine-Tuning. The model is fine-tuned with a contrastive objective built on AHAF-generated pairs, pulling correct image-text pairs together and pushing apart representations associated with hallucination-inducing perturbations. The important design choice is not merely the use of contrastive loss, but the controlled negative construction. Positive and negative samples share nearly all image content; the only systematic difference is the perturbation that flips the hallucination attribute. That makes the learning signal much more focused on the visual decision boundary.

AHAF also serves as a probe. If tiny pixel-level perturbations can flip the answer, then the visual representation is already sitting close to a fragile decision boundary even on clean inputs. That observation is more general than the specific method: many hallucination mitigation techniques may improve outputs without actually moving the underlying visual representation into a more stable region.

Compared with prior methods, VCD, OPERA, and VTI are more inference-time or post-hoc control methods; RLHF and DPO variants mainly reshape output preference; ordinary OCFT lacks targeted negatives. ACFT differs by directly training against the diagnosed visual misalignment mechanism, with no extra inference cost.8b:T7ee,The most informative evidence comes from three groups of experiments.

First, diagnostic evidence. On LLaVA v1.5, hallucinated samples show much worse image-text embedding alignment than correct samples: average cosine similarity is 0.158 for correct cases versus -0.122 for hallucinated ones. Grad-CAM analysis shows an inverted attention pattern. When the target object is present, hallucinated cases have more dispersed attention; when the object is absent, they show overly concentrated attention on irrelevant regions. Using normalized Shannon entropy over 500 hallucinated and 500 non-hallucinated samples, entropy is 5.1% higher for hallucinated cases when the object is present, and 6.2% lower when the object is absent. This supports a visual-perception failure rather than pure language-side fabrication.

Second, causal intervention. The paper perturbs the visual side directly. On POPE, adding Gaussian noise, downsampling the image, or replacing the visual encoder with a weaker one reduces average accuracy from 0.842 to the 0.739-0.822 range. Replacing it with a stronger SigLIP-SO400M encoder raises accuracy to 0.864. This is an important step beyond correlation: changing visual feature quality systematically changes hallucination behavior.

Third, mitigation results. ACFT uses only 0.9% of COCO for fine-tuning and outperforms VCD, OPERA, VTI, and post-training approaches such as LLaVA-RLHF and DPO variants on POPE and MME, while preserving general visual understanding. The full tables are not included in the provided excerpt, but the paper repeatedly emphasizes three properties: high data efficiency, zero inference overhead, and a clear gain over ordinary contrastive fine-tuning because the negatives are controlled rather than random.

For a careful read, the most useful experimental sections are the OCFT versus ACFT comparison, the target-versus-non-target similarity-gap analysis, and the encoder-strength ablations. Those explain why the method works, not just that it improves benchmark scores.8c:T509,Read it as a diagnosis-to-training paper. Start with the two findings and the causal validation in the introduction. The key question is whether the authors really close the loop from observation to intervention. Then go to the AHAF construction in the methods: how the PGD objective is defined, how the perturbation is constrained so it flips the hallucination attribute rather than destroying semantics, and how the paired samples enter the contrastive loss. That is where the paper either becomes a targeted hallucination method or collapses into generic adversarial robustness training.

In the experiments, prioritize four parts: the image-text similarity and Grad-CAM entropy analysis, the visual-side intervention studies, ACFT versus OCFT and prior mitigation methods, and the retention of general visual comprehension. If time is limited, Figures 1 to 3 and the main result tables are enough to capture the main argument in about 25 to 35 minutes.

Two deeper questions are worth keeping in mind. First, does AHAF mainly improve local robustness around adversarial boundaries, or does it genuinely improve broader visual alignment? Second, will the same mechanism hold for natively pretrained multimodal models, or is it especially suited to connector-style systems such as LLaVA?8d:T51f,The central method is LPS-TC, a lightweight proactive speech turn controller. It autoregressively consumes dual-channel audio streams from the user and the assistant, allowing it to model paralinguistic cues and interaction dynamics that text-only controllers miss. It is designed as a plug-and-play module rather than a replacement for the speech LLM: it can add full-duplex behavior to half-duplex systems or improve timing in existing full-duplex models. The action space includes Normal Turn Taking, Interruptive Turn Taking, Backchanneling, Barge In, and No Action. Normal Turn Taking and Backchanneling are further split into style labels derived from statistics such as silence duration, overlap duration, and action frequency. The paper also introduces WildTurn, an English dataset collected from real-world interactions, with span-based labels from conversational cues to response onset. GPT-5.2 is used to generate style-conditioned instructions. For evaluation, the authors argue that static prerecorded dialogues create context mismatch in multi-turn testing, since later user turns depend on the actual assistant response. They therefore split multi-round dialogues into individual turns with real preceding context and evaluate both chunk-level timing precision and turn-level interaction quality.8e:T8d1,全文的核心思路是把重复退化看成一个离散动力系统中的“入环”和“困环”问题，而不是把所有重复都归因于单步概率偏差。作者先用 coverage-based 的视角刻画 repetition loop：生成序列中往往存在一个短 N-gram 循环，覆盖了后续大部分 token。基于这个观察，他们把退化拆成两部分。

第一是 loop entry risk，也就是模型在某个关键上下文第一次踏入重复轨道的概率。作者发现这通常是一个 sharp entry event：只要在入环点替换掉少数几个高概率 token，后续轨迹就可能完全摆脱重复。第二是 loop persistence，即一旦进入循环，模型在连续多个时间步里持续留在循环中的倾向。作者指出 persistence 才是长程重复的主导项，因为它会在每一步累乘放大。

在这个分析上，论文进一步解释了为什么剪枝和朴素蒸馏会恶化问题。剪枝后的学生模型容量更紧，若仍用标准 distillation，它容易把概率质量泄漏到 teacher 原本压低的 token 上，这会提高 entry risk；同时它还会压扁 nucleus 内几个接近并列的合理候选，使模型更早承诺到单一路径，降低 escape mass，从而提高 persistence。这里的 escape mass 指的是在当前采样集合内，分配给“可接受但不重复”的替代 token 的总概率质量。

基于这两个失真来源，作者提出两个训练目标。FOCUS 用于抑制 leakage。它不是均匀模仿 teacher 全分布，而是对高置信 teacher 区域加权更高，让学生优先学稳 teacher 明确支持的 token，减少容量不足时向低支持区域漂移。RePAIR 用于降低 persistence。它围绕退化 onset 构造 continuation pair：一个是实际走向重复的 negative continuation，另一个是从同一起点重新生成得到的 non-degenerate continuation。然后用 margin-based objective 提升 onset 附近那些合理替代 token 的相对得分，增加 escape mass，避免模型过早锁死在循环轨道上。

从方法定位看，FOCUS 更像是改造蒸馏损失，RePAIR 更像是针对 loop-sensitive context 的对比式修复。两者互补：前者减少“误入”，后者增加“脱困”能力。8f:T96f,The central idea is to treat repetition as a dynamical process with two stages: entering a loop and staying in it. The paper adopts a coverage-based view of repetition loops, where a short recurring n-gram accounts for a large fraction of the generated continuation. Based on this, degeneration is decomposed into two quantities.

The first is loop entry risk: the probability that generation first falls into a repetitive trajectory at a sensitive context. The authors argue that this is often a sharp event. Replacing only a few high-probability tokens near the onset can be enough to divert the trajectory away from repetition. The second is loop persistence: once the model has entered the loop, how likely it is to remain there over successive decoding steps. Persistence is the dominant factor for long-horizon degeneration because it compounds across in-loop transitions.

This decomposition is then used to explain why pruning and naive distillation make the problem worse. Under reduced capacity, standard distillation can leak probability mass into tokens that the teacher had strongly suppressed, which raises entry risk. At the same time, it can collapse several plausible near-tie alternatives inside the nucleus set, causing the model to commit too early to a single path and reducing the escape mass available to non-repetitive continuations. Here, escape mass refers to the total probability assigned to acceptable alternative tokens that would let decoding leave the repetitive trajectory.

The paper proposes two complementary training objectives. FOCUS addresses leakage. Instead of matching the teacher distribution uniformly, it reweights distillation toward high-confidence teacher regions so that the student prioritizes tokens the teacher clearly supports, reducing drift into low-support regions. RePAIR addresses persistence. Around detected degeneration onsets, it constructs paired continuations: a repetitive negative continuation and a regenerated non-degenerate continuation from the same onset. A margin-based objective then increases the relative score of plausible alternatives near the onset, enlarging escape mass and reducing early commitment to the loop.

Conceptually, FOCUS is a distillation correction objective, while RePAIR is a contrastive repair objective for loop-sensitive contexts. They target different parts of the failure mode and are designed to be complementary.90:T6ba,Experiments are conducted in a post-pruning pipeline on Llama-family models, with LoRA-based finetuning after pruning. Evaluation covers both open-ended continuation on WikiText-103 and instruction-style generation on Self-Instruct. Importantly, the paper does not stop at perplexity. It also reports generation-quality and degeneration-sensitive metrics such as MAUVE, CREP, EAD, and semantic similarity measures including BERTScore.

The main empirical result is consistent: FOCUS and RePAIR reduce repetition and improve distributional and semantic quality, while incurring only a small increase in perplexity. The paper contrasts this with standard anti-repetition decoding heuristics, which can suppress repetition but often damage the language-model distribution and hurt coherence. The advantage here is that the method does not blindly penalize previously generated tokens; it selectively reshapes probability allocation at loop-sensitive contexts.

The most useful ablation-level insights are threefold. First, long-run degeneration is driven more by persistence than by the one-time entry event. Second, under nucleus decoding, preserving probability mass on several plausible alternatives is critical for avoiding lock-in to a repetitive trajectory. Third, FOCUS is compatible with existing training-based mitigation objectives and still improves generation quality when combined, suggesting that it addresses a relatively distinct source of distortion.

The abstract does not expose all numeric details, and the paper emphasizes consistency of trends more than a single headline number. When reading the results, the most informative view is the joint movement of repetition metrics, MAUVE/EAD, and perplexity.91:T488,A good reading order is: failure-mode decomposition, objective design, then empirical validation. Start with the introduction and the first half of the method section to understand why the authors separate degeneration into entry risk and persistence, and why escape mass matters. Then read the definitions of FOCUS and RePAIR carefully, paying attention to which distortion each one is meant to correct. Finally, inspect the main tables on WikiText-103 and Self-Instruct to see whether repetition reduction comes without a large loss in language quality.

If you only have 25 to 35 minutes, focus on four parts: the dynamical analysis of repetition loops, the reweighting logic in FOCUS, the paired-continuation construction in RePAIR, and the comparison against standard repetition-penalty style baselines in terms of perplexity and generation quality. For a deeper read, two follow-up questions are worth thinking about: whether this token-level guidance transfers to distillation, quantization recovery, or expert pruning in MoE models, and whether loop-sensitive contexts could be surfaced earlier as curriculum or hard-example signals during pretraining.92:T4d0,The method builds on Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation. The student is initialized from the domain-specialized model. A frozen copy of that model serves as the domain teacher, while the original open general model serves as the general teacher. The student samples trajectories on domain and general prompts, and the corresponding teacher evaluates each sampled token under the same prefix. The key quantity is the distillation advantage, defined as teacher log probability minus student log probability. Positive advantage increases the sampled token probability; negative advantage decreases it. The paper argues that standard MOPD suffers from two issues. First, ordinary on-policy sampling rarely exposes tokens with large positive teacher-student gaps, because samples come from the student distribution. Second, the advantage sign alone does not tell whether the update is safe. The proposed uncertainty-calibrated MOPD addresses these issues with dual-temperature sampling to broaden candidate trajectories, positive-advantage-density filtering to keep rollouts rich in high-gain tokens, and teacher-endorsement calibration to validate whether reinforcement or suppression is supported by the teacher’s own distribution.93:T50a,The paper first measures how instruction quality shapes the response distribution using Best-of-N and Worst-of-N analyses. It takes 1.5K UltraFeedback instructions, partitions them into High, Mid, and Low quality groups using rubric-based instruction scores, samples multiple responses with LLaMA3-8B, and scores them with a reward model. Best-of-N estimates the response-quality ceiling under a fixed sampling budget; Worst-of-N estimates the floor. High-quality instructions produce higher rewards on both sides, indicating that instruction quality affects not only the best available candidate but also the prevalence of trivial failures. The paper then relates this to DPO gradients: informative preference learning requires useful margins between chosen and rejected responses. Poor instructions can yield weak or trivial pairs, reducing the effective training signal. The proposed pipeline selects weak instructions using reward signals and revises them with rubric-guided LLM feedback. The revision is diagnostic rather than generic rewriting: the rubric targets ambiguity, missing constraints, underspecification, and comparability issues so that subsequent candidate responses become more informative. The pipeline keeps the examples instead of discarding low-quality instructions.94:T40c,SWE-Prime uses a two-stage, multi-granularity selection pipeline. Stage 1 operates at the trajectory level and keeps successful traces that are good in process quality, result quality, and representativeness. Process quality is measured from interaction logs using four signals: whether the trace follows an observe-edit-verify workflow, whether tool calls are reliable, whether there is continuous redundancy, and whether the trace uses Git-history leakage or similar shortcuts. Result quality favors minimal and sufficient patches. Representativeness prevents the selected set from collapsing to a narrow task type. Stage 2 operates at the semantic-segment level. Instead of judging isolated tool steps, it groups action-observation spans into behaviorally coherent segments and selects the segments that actually contribute to the final fix. During SFT, the full trajectory is kept as context, but only selected segments contribute to the loss. This avoids losing context while preventing low-value behavior from producing gradients.95:T404,Boundary-Calibrated Intervention Transfer, or BCIT, stores each update as a state-bound record: the source context, the observed source evidence, prespecified applicability conditions and named hard conflicts, and provenance links for the model, data, configuration, and evaluation artifacts. The decision is made for a pair consisting of one candidate and the current context. A non-compensable conflict leads to rejection. Insufficient or unresolved evidence triggers a bounded validation run from the current parent. Only candidates satisfying a frozen authorization rule receive the full training budget. A fully trained child is still subject to a separate promote-or-rollback rule. The system may generate a small number of new atomic proposals when progress stalls, but those proposals have no fabricated source evidence and cannot skip validation. The main distinction from simple experience replay is that an update is not labeled globally as good or bad; its evidence remains tied to the context where it was observed.96:T841,技术上分成两个层次。第一层是 PrivBoN。标准 BoN 是从基模型采样 n 个候选，用奖励模型打分后取 argmax。作者在每个候选分数上加入独立 Gumbel 噪声，尺度设为 sigma=2Δr/ε，其中 Δr 是奖励模型对相邻偏好数据集的敏感度。这样做有两个效果：从隐私角度，它等价于指数机制，直接给出 ε-DP；从优化角度，带 Gumbel 噪声的 argmax 在大样本极限下对应 softmax 选择，也就是求解一个 KL 正则化的最优策略。论文进一步把这个 regularization 强度与 Huang 等人关于 BoN regret skyline 的理论接起来，证明当隐私预算超过阈值 ε*(x) 时，DP 所要求的噪声强度正好落在 regret 最优区间，因此不会额外损伤对齐。

第二层是 PrivITP。PrivBoN 的问题在于“隐私免费”的阈值依赖未知的 coverage coefficient C^{π*}，实际系统无法验证。为此作者提出 private inference-time pessimism：先用 χ² 正则化的 rejection sampling 构造更保守的选择分布，再用两阶段 Gaussian 机制实现近似 DP。这里的关键不是简单加高斯噪声，而是把基于 ReLU 的拒绝采样重写成 randomized-threshold mechanism，从而得到一个与候选数 n 无关、只依赖实际 halting time 的 ex-post DP 保证。理论分析里还有一个重要工具：smoothed-weight policy comparison lemma，用策略权重函数的 ℓ∞ 距离控制 value gap，于是 regret 可以分解成奖励模型误差项和隐私噪声项，形式上是 O(sqrt(C^{π*}(ε_RM^2 + R_max σ)))。这比直接分析 noisy argmax 更细，因为它把 privacy cost 单独拆了出来，也解释了为什么 PrivITP 在未知 coverage 情况下更稳。

从方法取舍看，作者没有走训练时 DP-RM 或 DP-RLHF 的路线，因为目标是冻结模型、服务时对齐；也没有只做 heuristic smoothing，因为那样没有正式隐私保证。选择 Gumbel/指数机制和 Gaussian 两阶段机制，都是为了把 selection rule 写成可证明的随机机制，而不是把隐私当作附带噪声工程。97:T87e,The method has two layers.

The first is Private Best-of-N (PrivBoN). Standard BoN samples n candidates from a base policy, scores them with a reward model, and returns the argmax. PrivBoN adds i.i.d. Gumbel noise to each reward score with scale sigma = 2Δr/ε, where Δr is the reward-model sensitivity under neighboring preference datasets. This gives ε-differential privacy because noisy argmax with Gumbel noise is equivalent to the exponential mechanism. More interestingly, in the large-n limit the same mechanism implements a KL-regularized alignment optimum: the induced selection rule becomes a softmax policy over rewards. The paper then connects this regularization strength to the regret skyline from prior BoN theory, showing that when the privacy budget exceeds a critical threshold ε*(x), the privacy-imposed noise is exactly in the regret-optimal range. In that regime, privacy is effectively free from an alignment-regret perspective.

The second is Private Inference-Time Pessimism (PrivITP). PrivBoN depends on an unknown coverage coefficient C^{π*}, so the favorable threshold cannot be verified in practice. PrivITP addresses this by combining χ²-regularized rejection sampling with a two-phase Gaussian mechanism. The key move is not simply adding Gaussian noise, but reformulating a ReLU-based rejection sampler as a randomized-threshold mechanism. That yields an ex-post approximate-DP guarantee whose bound is independent of the candidate count n and depends only on the realized halting time. The regret analysis uses a smoothed-weight policy comparison lemma that controls value gaps through the ℓ∞ distance between policy weight functions, leading to a bound of the form O(sqrt(C^{π*}(ε_RM^2 + R_max σ))). This cleanly separates reward-model error from privacy cost and explains why PrivITP is more robust when coverage is unknown.

A notable design choice is that the paper does not solve the problem by retraining the reward model with DP or by using heuristic smoothing. It treats inference-time selection itself as the object of study and chooses mechanisms whose stochasticity is analytically tied to both privacy and alignment.98:T5b6,The empirical study spans four reward models, two language models of different sizes, and three benchmark families: GSM8K, MMLU, and MATH. The main findings are consistent with the theory.

1. Standard BoN is not scaling-monotonic under reward-model error. As N increases, performance can peak and then degrade, which is the practical signature of reward hacking.
2. PrivBoN mitigates this failure mode. With theoretically calibrated Gumbel noise, the performance curve as a function of N becomes much more stable, and the method preserves the benefit of test-time compute without over-amplifying reward-model error.
3. PrivITP consistently matches or outperforms PrivBoN at comparable privacy levels, especially in regimes where large candidate sets make BoN more brittle.
4. In multi-query deployment, the ex-post composition structure matters. When combined with the FSRC accounting framework, PrivITP can answer substantially more queries under a fixed privacy budget than standard worst-case composition.

The most informative part of the experiments is not any single headline number, but the shape of the scaling curves: whether BoN degrades at large N, whether the private mechanisms restore monotonicity or at least suppress the pathology, and whether the observed privacy-performance tradeoff matches the threshold story from the theory. If the full paper provides tables with ε, N, query counts, and task metrics, those are the right axes to inspect.99:T527,Start with Sections 3 and 4, then return to the introduction once the mechanisms are clear. Four parts deserve attention.

First, read the equivalence between Gumbel-noisy argmax and the exponential mechanism. That is the bridge that makes PrivBoN simultaneously a DP mechanism and a KL-regularized selector.

Second, inspect the derivation and meaning of the critical threshold ε*(x). This is where the paper ties privacy, reward-model error, and coverage together, and it also reveals why PrivBoN alone is not operationally sufficient.

Third, read the reformulation lemma and the ex-post DP proof for PrivITP carefully. If you work on adaptive compute, test-time search, or verifier-guided reranking, this part is likely the most reusable.

Fourth, focus on the scaling plots and the composition experiments rather than only final averages. The central empirical question is whether the private mechanisms prevent the large-N failure mode and how much budget is saved in repeated-query settings.

Although tagged as skim, the theory sections are worth a deeper read if your interests include reward-model serving or the interface between post-training and deployment. A fast pass through the introduction, core theorems, and figures should take about 45 minutes; a full technical read is closer to 1.5 to 2.5 hours.9a:T864,方法上，这不是提出全新 ES 变体，而是对 ES 作为 reasoning post-training 工具做系统分析，并与 GRPO 做机制层面对照。ES 的基本过程是：对当前参数加随机扰动，得到一组 perturbed policies；每个扰动模型只做前向采样和 verifier 打分；再把 reward-weighted perturbations 聚合成更新方向。它绕开反向传播，因此显存占用低、并行性强。GRPO 则是在单一策略上采样多条响应，用组内相对优势构造 token-level policy gradient 更新。

作者的理论部分聚焦于“为什么 ES 可能有更高 Pass@K”。核心概念是 verifier-projected Jensen-Shannon diversity：不是看表面文本多样性，而是看 ES 群体在 verifier 视角下覆盖了多少不同的有效推理模式。论文论证这种群体多样性有助于 repeated sampling success，并且可以转化为更新后策略更高的 Pass@K。这个角度很关键，因为它把 ES 的优势从“无梯度优化也能训”转成“参数空间探索保留了解空间覆盖”。

经验分析部分主要有三块。第一，作者比较 ES 与 GRPO 的熵动态和 reasoning coverage，指出 GRPO 会出现 entropy collapse，而 ES 没有同样程度的收缩。第二，作者分析 ES 的参数变化分布，发现真正与任务相关的效果集中在少量较大幅度更新上，而大量参数变化在 perturbation cancellation 后功能贡献很小，因此 whole-model drift 不能直接等价为 widespread functional change。第三，作者系统扫超参数和估计器设计，结论包括：z-score reward normalization 是 ES 成功训练的关键；在 reasoning 的离散 reward 场景下，zeroth-order SFT 常用的 two-point estimator 并不带来优势；随着 pretrained model 规模增大，达到有效优化所需的 population size 反而下降。

论文还提出两个顺序组合方案 ES→GRPO 和 GRPO→ES，用来结合 GRPO 在 Pass@1 上的优势与 ES 在 Pass@K 上的优势。这不是特别复杂的算法创新，但很实用，因为它把两种更新机制看成对策略分布施加不同偏置的阶段性工具。9b:T9c4,This is not primarily a new ES algorithm; it is a systematic mechanistic study of ES as a reasoning post-training paradigm, with GRPO as the main gradient-based comparator. In ES, the current parameters are perturbed to form a population of policies, each perturbed model is evaluated by forward-only sampling and verifier rewards, and reward-weighted perturbations are aggregated into an update estimate. This avoids backpropagation, making ES memory-efficient and easy to parallelize. GRPO, in contrast, samples multiple responses from a single policy and applies a token-level policy-gradient-style update based on relative advantages within the group.

The theoretical contribution centers on why ES may achieve higher Pass@K. The paper introduces verifier-projected Jensen-Shannon diversity, which measures diversity not at the surface-text level but in terms of distinct reasoning modes that matter under the verifier. The argument is that higher diversity across the ES population increases repeated-sampling success and can translate into higher Pass@K in the updated policy. This is an important framing shift: the advantage of ES is not just that it is zeroth-order, but that population-based parameter-space exploration preserves broader solution coverage.

Empirically, the paper analyzes three aspects. First, it compares entropy dynamics and reasoning coverage under ES and GRPO, showing that GRPO exhibits entropy collapse while ES does not collapse in the same way. Second, it studies the distribution of parameter changes under ES and finds that task-relevant effects are concentrated in a small subset of larger-magnitude updates, while much of the overall drift contributes little after perturbation cancellation. This supports the claim that whole-model drift is not the same as widespread functional change. Third, it performs a systematic sweep over hyperparameters and estimator variants, finding that z-score reward normalization is critical, that the two-point estimator commonly used in zeroth-order SFT offers no benefit under discrete reasoning rewards, and that the population size needed for effective optimization decreases as pretrained model scale increases.

The paper also proposes two sequential compositions, ES→GRPO and GRPO→ES, to combine GRPO’s strength on Pass@1 with ES’s strength on Pass@K. The idea is simple but useful: the two methods impose different biases on the policy distribution and can be staged rather than treated as mutually exclusive.9c:T58b,From the full text provided, the main experiments are conducted on GSM8K and DeepScaleR, comparing ES against GRPO on Pass@1, Pass@K, entropy dynamics, capability retention, and hyperparameter sensitivity. The main empirical result is that ES improves Pass@1 while achieving higher Pass@K than GRPO, and it does so without the same degree of entropy collapse. In effect, GRPO tends to sharpen the policy around a smaller set of successful reasoning trajectories, whereas ES preserves a broader set of viable paths.

On capability preservation, the paper reports that under appropriate training settings, held-out capabilities remain largely intact. Combined with the parameter-change analysis, this supports the claim that previously observed forgetting under ES is better explained by training-set overfitting than by parameter drift per se.

The hyperparameter study yields several practical takeaways: z-score reward normalization is a key ingredient for successful ES training; the two-point estimator does not help in reasoning tasks with discrete verifier rewards; and larger pretrained models require smaller population sizes for effective ES optimization. For deeper reading, inspect how reasoning coverage is operationalized, which held-out capabilities are used, and whether the claim that required population size decreases with model scale holds consistently across model families.9e:T91c,RubricRM is a pairwise generative reward model. The input is an instruction q and two candidate images I_A and I_B; image editing additionally includes a source image. Instead of directly predicting which image is better, the model generates a structured rubric and dimension-level assessments for both candidates in one pass. The rubric includes task intent, atomic evaluation dimensions d_i, weights w_i over those dimensions, and scoring criteria L_i for each dimension. The model then assigns per-dimension scores s_i^k to each image, aggregates them with the learned weights, and derives the final preference from the weighted totals.

The key design choice is not merely to produce free-form rationales, but to turn explanation into a structured scoring protocol. That makes the output more controllable and allows training signals to operate at the dimension level rather than only at the final pairwise label.

Training has two stages. In the SFT stage, the model learns rubric trajectories synthesized by a teacher: how to decompose the instruction into intent, dimensions, weights, criteria, and then score the candidates. In the RL stage, the paper uses dimension-level GRPO. The objective aligns predicted score differences with reference score differences on each rubric dimension, and penalizes preference-direction reversals more strongly. This indicates that the authors care not only about final pairwise accuracy but also about the internal correctness of the dimension-wise judgment process.

Data construction is a major part of the contribution. The paper argues that dynamic rubric learning requires broad instruction coverage; otherwise the model will learn biased rubric templates and generalize poorly. To address this, the authors aggregate multiple open-source preference datasets, analyze instruction types for text-to-image generation and image editing, define classification criteria, and use DeepSeek-V3.2 for automatic taxonomy annotation. They then perform balanced sampling, identify underrepresented categories, synthesize additional prompts for those categories, generate candidate images, collect expert preference annotations, and finally synthesize rubric trajectories for each preference sample. The resulting training sets contain 31.8K text-to-image samples and 30.7K image-editing samples.9f:T54f,The experiments train dedicated models for text-to-image generation and image editing on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones. If deciding whether to follow up, check two things first: the gain over fixed-dimension reward models, and whether dimension-level RL actually improves final pairwise preference accuracy.a1:T8c1,方法设计很克制，核心是“保留标准 student update，只在严格筛选的条件下做 student-to-teacher adaptation”。训练仍然从 student on-policy rollout 开始：student 只看题目 x 采样解答 y，teacher 在同一条 partial rollout 上、但额外看到参考解 y*，输出逐 token 分布。标准 OPSD 部分不变，student 继续用 teacher 的 token-level target 做蒸馏更新。VISTA 新增的是 teacher 更新，而且只在两层筛选后发生。

第一层是 rollout-level gating。只有当 student rollout 通过 outcome verifier 时，这条 rollout 才被认为包含了值得 teacher 学习的 problem-only reasoning 轨迹。这里的判断不是“student 比 teacher 强”，而是“这条 rollout 至少在结果上成立，因此其中某些 student token 偏好可能比 reference-conditioned teacher 更贴近部署时可行的推理分布”。这样做避免把 teacher 拉向明显错误的 student 行为。

第二层是 token-level selection。即便 rollout 最终正确，也不意味着整条序列的每个位置都该拿来更新 teacher。论文用 teacher-student disagreement 的 KL 信号做位置选择，只在 top-k 个分歧最大的 token 位置上，把 teacher 向 student 适度拉近。这里的直觉很重要：真正需要修正的是 teacher 最不贴近 problem-only reasoning 的位置，而不是所有位置。若全序列都更新，teacher 很快会塌缩到 student，失去 privileged knowledge，后续也就无法继续提供互补监督。

从损失形式看，VISTA 复用了标准 OPSD 的同类蒸馏损失，没有再造一个复杂目标。它的创新不在 loss 公式本身，而在“哪些 rollout 能作为 teacher 反馈”“哪些 token 位置值得反馈”这两个选择机制。论文还把这一设计与已有方法区分得比较清楚：RLSD 是在 student 侧用 verifier reward 约束更新方向；TRACE 是限制 distillation 的 token span；DemoPSD 是在 teacher-student disagreement 时重加权 student target。它们都在减少 student 受坏 teacher 影响，但 teacher 本身仍是静态的。VISTA 则让 teacher 在受控条件下被 student 的成功行为校准，因此改变的是监督源本身。a2:T4a5,The main significance is conceptual and methodological. Conceptually, the paper reframes privileged distillation as a target-alignment problem rather than a simple stronger-model-supervises-weaker-model setup. That matters beyond reasoning post-training. Any setting with a conditioning gap between teacher and student—reference-conditioned teachers, tool-augmented teachers, retrieval-conditioned teachers, multimodal teachers supervising text-only students—faces the same issue. Methodologically, VISTA introduces a controlled feedback loop from student to teacher without discarding the standard OPSD student update. This is a meaningful contribution because it changes the supervision source itself, not just the student's robustness to bad supervision. Empirically, the gains are consistent across three Qwen3 scales, and the method stays lightweight: no extra sampling and no separate RL objective. For researchers working on pretrain/post-train interfaces, the useful lesson is that supervision quality depends not only on teacher capability, but also on whether the teacher distribution is calibrated to the student's observable information and feasible reasoning trajectories.a3:T9b5,VISTA keeps the standard OPSD pipeline intact and adds a tightly controlled student-to-teacher adaptation step. Training still begins with an on-policy student rollout: the student policy sees only the problem x and samples a solution y, while the teacher sees both x and the reference solution y*. Both models are evaluated on the same partial student rollout. The student update remains unchanged: it is still distilled toward the teacher's token-level distribution, exactly as in standard OPSD.

The new part is the teacher update, and it is gated twice.

First, VISTA applies rollout-level selection using an outcome verifier. Only student rollouts that pass verification are allowed to provide feedback to the teacher. The logic is not that the student is globally better than the teacher, but that a verified rollout contains evidence that some of the student's token-level preferences are compatible with successful problem-only reasoning. This prevents the teacher from being pulled toward clearly bad student behavior.

Second, VISTA applies token-level selection within each eligible rollout. Even a correct rollout should not be used wholesale. The paper computes teacher-student disagreement and selects the top-k positions with the largest KL discrepancy. Teacher adaptation is applied only at those sparse positions. This is the central design choice. The goal is to correct the teacher exactly where its distribution is most misaligned with successful problem-only reasoning, while preserving the rest of the teacher's privileged knowledge. If the teacher were updated densely across all positions, the teacher-student gap would collapse too quickly and the teacher would lose its complementary value as a privileged supervisor.

An important practical point is that VISTA reuses the same rollouts and the same family of distillation losses as standard OPSD. The novelty is not a new reward function or a complicated optimization objective. It lies in deciding which rollouts are trustworthy for teacher feedback and which token positions are worth adapting. This also distinguishes VISTA from prior methods. RLSD constrains student updates with verifier rewards; TRACE restricts distillation to selected spans; DemoPSD reweights the target toward the student when teacher and student disagree. All of them reduce student exposure to mismatched teacher targets, but the teacher remains static. VISTA instead calibrates the teacher itself using verified student behavior.a4:T83a,The main experiments cover three Qwen3 model scales—1.7B, 4B, and 8B—on three competition-math benchmarks under a matched OPSD protocol. Relative to reported OPSD, the average improves by 0.6, 0.7, and 2.1 points at 1.7B, 4B, and 8B respectively. At step t, a standard gradient-based proposer generates a batch of suffix candidates from the current suffix. The baseline strategy evaluates each candidate with the current attack loss and keeps the lowest-loss one. TACS replaces this with a richer scoring rule built from three kinds of signals.

The first is the standard current-step quality term, L_now, typically the target-token cross-entropy over the training behavior set. This remains in the score because immediate optimization quality still matters.

The second is trajectory-aware information. From the provided text, two components are central. One is an auxiliary early-token loss, denoted as something like L_first, computed only on the beginning of the target response. The motivation is intuitive: jailbreak failure often reappears at the start of the answer, where refusal templates or safety scaffolds come back first. A candidate that already supports the early part of the harmful response may therefore be more promising than one with a slightly lower average loss. The other is a one-step improvement proxy, Δ1(a), intended to estimate whether a candidate leaves room for useful future progress rather than merely fitting the current step. Even without the full formula, the design intent is clear: score candidates by downstream search utility, not just current proxy fit.

The third ingredient is reference regularization. Inspired by ideas from ORPO-style regularized optimization, TACS stabilizes selection by comparing against a reference signal or reference distribution. The role here is not alignment in the usual sense, but preventing the selector from making overly aggressive moves based on noisy or misleading local proxy improvements.

An important practical point is that TACS does not require extra intermediate model queries and does not assume access to a true reward. It only reuses signals already available in standard suffix optimization. Relative to prior jailbreak work, the novelty is in the selector rather than the proposer. Relative to ordinary reranking, the target is not better single-step ranking but better multi-step search trajectories.aa:T506,The main empirical claim is that, under the same search budget, changing only the candidate selector improves average attack success rate on HarmBench by nearly 10%. If you work on RLHF, preference optimization, search-based data synthesis, or red-teaming, the paper is interesting because it makes reward hacking concrete at the selector level.ac:T524,The method is Adaptive Multi-Reward Projection, or AMRP. Instead of using a fixed weighted sum of reward dimensions throughout training, AMRP updates the projection weights online based on training dynamics. It uses three signals.

The first is relative shortfall, which measures whether a reward dimension is lagging behind the others. If a dimension remains under-optimized, its weight is increased. The second is reward volatility, which tracks instability in a dimension. High volatility suggests that the policy has not stabilized there, so AMRP keeps attention on it. The third is recent progress, which measures whether a dimension is improving, stagnating, or regressing. Saturated and stable dimensions get down-weighted; stagnant or regressing dimensions get up-weighted.

This design addresses the two identified failure modes in a practical way. It does not eliminate the information loss of scalarization entirely, but it reduces persistent aliasing by making the projection time-varying rather than static. More importantly, it counters shortcut lock-in by reallocating learning pressure toward neglected dimensions. Compared with manual reward tuning or simple normalization, the key difference is that AMRP is driven by observed reward dynamics during training rather than by fixed prior assumptions.ad:T4a0,The evaluation covers three multi-reward settings: rule-based mathematical reasoning, citation-grounded generation with automatic evaluators, and open-ended alignment using learned reward-model scores. The paper also provides mechanism-level evidence. It shows that under static aggregation, training is often dominated early by dense rewards such as format or length, while harder dimensions such as correctness remain under-optimized. AMRP changes the reward-profile dynamics by shifting weight toward lagging or unstable dimensions, which leads to more balanced profiles over time. Another useful result is compatibility: the method composes with PPO, GRPO, and GDPO, suggesting that it is best viewed as a reward-aggregation module rather than a replacement for the RL optimizer itself. The emphasis is less on one dramatic benchmark number and more on consistent gains plus healthier reward trajectories.ae:T793,The method, TUSA, inserts a training-free cognitive arbiter between the base model policy πθ and the weak specialist πϕ. Instead of combining the two distributions at every step, the system first lets the base model propose a candidate token and then decides whether the specialist is allowed to intervene. The decision is made by a gate defined through a Joint Necessity Score.

That score combines two signals. The first is supervisor confidence, operationalized mainly through token-level entropy of the specialist distribution. Low entropy means the specialist has a sharper belief over the next token and is more likely to provide meaningful guidance. The second is semantic saliency. The paper argues that many decoding positions carry little semantic load, so spending intervention budget on function words or low-information tokens is wasteful even if the specialist is confident there.

The arbiter activates only when both conditions hold: the specialist is confident enough, and the current token is semantically important enough. This is stronger than a plain entropy threshold. Confidence alone would still trigger many low-value interventions; saliency alone would allow the specialist to overwrite the base model even when it is unsure. Their conjunction turns alignment into trust-based arbitration rather than continuous supervision.

Conceptually, the contribution is less about a new learned reward model and more about a new control logic at decoding time. Compared with dense guidance methods such as MARA-style token-level steering, TUSA changes three things: intervention becomes event-triggered rather than always-on; authorization depends on uncertainty-aware gating rather than fixed fusion; and the objective shifts from maximizing supervision coverage to minimizing harmful low-confidence interference. In that sense, the method is closer to abstention and selective prediction than to stronger supervision.af:T630,The experiments address two questions: whether weak specialists are indeed persistently uncertain, and whether sparse intervention outperforms dense intervention. Second, the trade-off between intervention rate and preference/safety outcomes. Third, the ablations comparing full TUSA against entropy-only, saliency-only, and threshold variants.
