A deeper read should examine whether entropy is a sufficient proxy for local supervisory competence, and whether the same arbitration logic could be extended to verifier-guided decoding, reward models, or multi-supervisor systems.b1:T671,OSW-FT keeps the standard expert trajectory as the optimization target, but rescales its loss online. For each query q, the current model runs K inference-only rollouts to estimate a pass rate p-hat(q). The usual SFT loss on the expert output o* is then multiplied by (1 - p-hat(q)). Queries the model already solves reliably get downweighted; unresolved frontier queries get larger updates.

The design choice is important. The method does not optimize on sampled trajectories, does not apply token-level reward shaping, and does not alter the training distribution. The rollout is used only to estimate a scalar weight. This sharply separates it from PPO/GRPO-style methods, where the sampled trajectories both define the learning signal and receive the update.

The theoretical framing is built for binary-verifiable reasoning. The authors start from expected correctness, apply the score-function trick, and introduce a query-dependent control variate. This yields a variance-reduced estimator whose optimal baseline depends on the model’s success probability on that query. That connection motivates why scaling the expert log-likelihood gradient by a function of success rate is sensible. They further argue that with finite K, the Monte Carlo estimate remains unbiased for the exact OSW-FT surrogate update, so rollout noise affects variance but not the target update itself.

Conceptually, this is best read as online difficulty-aware SFT rather than offline RL or reward-weighted regression. The online component estimates whether an example is still informative; the offline expert trajectory still specifies what the model should learn.b2:T5a9,The experiments use Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 4B parameters on binary-verifiable reasoning benchmarks including AIME, AMC, MATH-500, and GPQA-Diamond. The empirical claim is deliberately modest: OSW-FT consistently improves over standard SFT at small-to-medium scales, but it is not presented as a universal replacement for GRPO.

The results support four main points. First, adaptive online weighting beats uniform SFT across multiple model sizes, which suggests that competence-aware reweighting is useful even when the supervision target stays fixed. Second, under limited rollout budgets, OSW-FT often offers a better compute-performance trade-off because it only needs a few inference-only samples per query and avoids the full RL optimization loop. Third, the comparison with GRPO is mixed in the expected way: OSW-FT is favorable in several low-budget settings, while GRPO remains stronger in some configurations. Fourth, the ablations matter: continuous success-rate weighting outperforms hard-thresholding and random weighting, indicating that the gain comes from a smooth online estimate of current competence rather than generic sample reweighting.

The provided full text excerpt does not include all table values, so exact benchmark deltas are not fully recoverable here. Still, the paper is clear about the pattern it wants to establish: consistent gains over SFT across 0.6B–4B models, especially when rollout budget is constrained.b3:T486,The paper connects MH acceptance ratios to Bradley–Terry (BT) choice models. Under BT, the odds of preferring x over y equal exp(u(x)-u(y)), which matches the unnormalized density ratio needed by MH for a Gibbs target. The obstacle is that the algorithm cannot query the comparison probability itself—only draw Bernoulli preference samples. The authors prove an impossibility result: any fixed-budget plug-in estimator of the acceptance ratio (estimate win probabilities then substitute into MH) cannot implement the oracle acceptance rule and can arbitrarily distort the stationary distribution. Pref-MH avoids estimating probabilities and instead designs a randomized accept/reject mechanism whose marginal acceptance probability exactly matches the Hastings ratio implied by the preference odds (plus proposal correction). With this construction, detailed balance holds in expectation, yielding an exact stationary distribution while using only a fixed number of binary comparisons per transition. The method is stated for general state spaces and arbitrary proposal kernels, positioning it as a general-purpose MCMC wrapper around preference oracles.b4:T4b6,The proposed mechanism is trait-direction drift:
- Define a teacher-side preference gap for each sample (p,r) as the log-likelihood difference between a biased system prompt and a set of neutral prompts, with a length-normalized variant to compare variable-length completions.
- Use an empirically motivated low-rank/logit-linear factorization of the prompt-by-sample log-probability matrix (via SVD-like geometry): prompt embeddings ψ(s) and sample embeddings φ(p,r) explain why certain “innocent” samples still carry trait signal.
- Argue (and test) that student SFT updates contain a component aligned with a recognizable trait direction; across steps this component accumulates beyond noise, producing measurable drift and eventually behavioral transfer (preference shifts or higher misalignment rates).
- Introduce probe-space corridor regularization: monitor the student’s coordinate along a probed trait/steering subspace and penalize deviations outside a corridor, limiting motion along the trait direction while keeping general task learning largely intact.
The paper also studies why cross-model subliminal transfer is weaker than same-model transfer, using diagnostics and interventions.b5:T897,方法叫 FactAgent，核心由两部分组成：fact-centric agent state，以及基于 Bayesian fact utility estimation 的 dense process supervision。

先看 agent 形式。与标准 ReAct 只维护原始对话和工具返回文本不同，FactAgent 在状态里显式维护一个 fact store。每次 search 动作得到 observation 后，agent 不只是继续推理，还可以执行 assert 动作，把 observation 里的信息抽取成结构化事实，写入 fact store。这样，状态从“越来越长的文本历史”变成“问题 Q、当前 observation、累计事实集合 Ft”。作者把这些事实视为离散语义单元，而不是普通字符串，这一步是后续 credit assignment 的基础。

再看奖励构造。论文的关键不是直接给 assert 打启发式分，而是从 group rollouts 里估计事实的后验效用。具体做法是先把语义等价的事实聚成 cluster，避免同一证据因表述不同被分散统计；然后基于一组 rollout 的最终 outcome，用 Bayesian estimation 推断每个 fact cluster 与成功结果的统计关联。直观上，如果某类事实经常出现在成功轨迹里、较少出现在失败轨迹里，它的 posterior utility 就更高。随后，这个 fact-level utility 被映射回 step-level dense rewards，用来训练 policy。

这比直接做 token-level process reward 更适合搜索任务，因为搜索任务的有效中间单位不是 token，也不一定是整句 reasoning，而是“找到并确认了哪条证据”。作者因此把 credit assignment 的对象从 action surface form 转成 evidence semantics。和纯 outcome-based GRPO 相比，FactAgent 仍然利用 group rollouts，但不再让整条轨迹共享同一个粗粒度 advantage，而是通过事实聚类和后验估计，把奖励分配到真正有贡献的中间步骤上。

从设计取舍看，这个方法避免了额外训练 reward model，也不依赖人工标注每一步是否正确，代价则是需要可靠的事实抽取与聚类。如果抽取质量差，后验 utility 估计会被噪声污染。全文也承认这一点，因此 fact store 既是方法优势，也是误差传播的主要入口。b6:T89d,FactAgent has two main components: a fact-centric state representation and a Bayesian utility estimation scheme for dense process supervision.

On the agent side, the paper departs from standard ReAct-style agents that keep only raw text history. The state explicitly includes a fact store. After a search action returns an observation, the agent can take an assert action that extracts structured facts from the observation and writes them into the store. The state is therefore represented as the question, the current observation, and the accumulated fact set. These facts are treated as discrete semantic evidence units rather than plain text snippets. This is important because the method assigns credit at the level of evidence semantics, not at the level of surface-form actions.

On the reward side, the paper estimates fact utility from grouped rollouts. Semantically equivalent facts are first clustered so that the same evidence is not split across multiple textual variants. Then, using final outcomes from a group of trajectories, the method performs Bayesian estimation of the posterior utility of each fact cluster. Intuitively, if a fact cluster appears disproportionately often in successful trajectories, its posterior utility increases. These fact-level utilities are then converted into dense step-level rewards for policy optimization.

This differs from standard outcome-based GRPO, where all steps in a trajectory inherit the same coarse trajectory-level signal. Here, group rollouts are still used, but the reward is redistributed through an explicit evidence layer. That makes the method better matched to search tasks, where the meaningful intermediate unit is often not a token or a reasoning sentence, but a retrieved and validated piece of evidence.

The design also avoids training an external reward model and does not require human annotation of intermediate steps. The trade-off is that the whole pipeline depends on the quality of fact extraction and fact clustering. If those are noisy, the posterior utility estimates can be corrupted. The paper is aware of this: the fact store is both the main strength of the method and the main source of possible error propagation.b7:T5ef,The experiments use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbones and evaluate on seven QA benchmarks. The headline result is that with the 7B backbone, FactAgent reaches an average EM of 51.2, outperforming the strongest baseline by +3.2 EM. The paper emphasizes that the gains are consistent across benchmarks rather than driven by a single dataset.

The more informative findings come from the analysis. The dense process supervision mainly improves evidence precision and retrieval quality. That matches the method design: the reward does not simply encourage more search, but encourages finding useful evidence and committing it into the explicit state.

The ablations likely cover the main components: removing the fact store, removing the assert action, disabling fact clustering, or replacing Bayesian posterior utility with simpler statistics. From the full-text description, the explicit fact representation and the utility estimation module are the most important contributors. Another practical point is that the method derives dense rewards directly from grouped rollout outcomes, without relying on an external reward model, which makes the training setup lighter and easier to scale.

The current evidence mainly supports search-heavy QA agents. Whether the same approach transfers to broader web agents, coding agents, or longer-horizon multi-tool settings depends on whether “facts” remain the right intermediate abstraction and whether fact extraction stays reliable in those environments.b8:T427,Start with the introduction and preliminaries to see that the paper changes more than the reward function. It jointly changes the state representation, the action space, and the reward decomposition. Then focus on three technical pieces: how the fact store is defined, how the assert action extracts and writes facts, and how Bayesian utility estimation is computed from grouped rollouts. The key questions while reading are: what exactly counts as a fact, how semantic equivalence is handled, and how posterior fact utility is mapped back to step-level rewards.

In the experiments, prioritize the main results table, the analyses on evidence precision and retrieval quality, and the ablations on fact store and utility estimation. A skim in about 40 minutes is enough to capture the main idea. A deeper read should ask whether explicit intermediate state could replace part of free-form chain-of-thought in reasoning RL, and whether fact-level credit assignment could generalize to code execution states, web interaction states, or multimodal tool trajectories.b9:T53e,The method has two main components. The evaluation pipeline samples from roughly 100k monthly production queries while balancing diversity and representativeness. Uniform sampling preserves the production distribution but keeps many near-duplicate templates. Diversity-first sampling increases coverage but distorts the service and task mix. The paper introduces a template-aware sampler: mask variable spans, cluster near-identical normalized prompts with LSH, select diverse examples within each template using greedy max-min over variable spans, and allocate budget proportional to the square root of template count. Scoring is task-specific. Classification and information extraction, about 63.2% of traffic, use reference-based evaluation with gold answers generated by Kimi-K2.5 and checked by annotators. Open-ended summarization and generation use side-by-side judging augmented with checklist-style rubrics. The training recipe starts from Qwen3-32B with a Cyrillic-dense tokenizer and runs in non-reasoning mode for latency and cost reasons. It performs a combined SFT stage, then trains separate GRPO experts for instruction following, function calling, and internal task-distribution alignment. The experts are merged with two-stage SLERP in weight space to avoid cross-domain reward interference from a single joint RL objective.ba:T4a5,The deployed adapted model absorbed 50% of platform traffic six months after rollout, corresponding to 116 million requests per month from more than 200 internal applications. On benchmark construction, the template-aware sampler reaches a mean pairwise TF-IDF cosine distance of 0.953 while keeping Jensen-Shannon distances lower than pure diversity sampling, indicating better coverage without strongly drifting from production mix. For judging, a uniform side-by-side LLM judge has limited agreement with experts, with Cohen’s kappa around 0.62 and task-dependent errors. After task routing, the LLM task classifier matches human consensus 90.6% to 99.6% of the time. The final task-specific judging pipeline improves agreement: reference-based subtasks rise from kappa 0.63 to 0.88, and open-ended content-generation subtasks rise from 0.57 to 0.72. The 5MB and 10MB data tiers use 39M-parameter models, while the 100MB and 1000MB tiers use 125M-parameter models. The models have disjoint vocabularies, parameters, and corpora. The authors also replicate the effect on five independently developed monolingual models around 1B parameters. A GlotLID-v3 audit reports at most about 0.1% English content in the non-English corpora used in the main analysis. Evaluation uses FLORES-200, Tatoeba, OPUS, and BouQUET over 36 language pairs. Matched parallel sentences consistently show higher CKA than shuffled controls across layers and language pairs. On FLORES with SGPT pooling, last-layer matched CKA averages about 0.78, versus about 0.17 for the shuffled baseline. Alignment becomes stronger with larger data, larger models, and closer languages. A Procrustes rotation is sufficient for useful alignment; affine and MLP mappings lower reconstruction error but hurt retrieval. In causal patching, rotated English residuals often flip a target-language model’s factual cloze prediction to the donor capital, with the effect holding across five unrelated target languages and approaching the within-model patching ceiling.bc:T7b8,SCIT，Suffix Cache Interchange Test，本质上是一个 cache-level counterfactual intervention protocol。给定 recipient 问题 r 和 source 问题 s，先构造一个精确可验证的反事实：source 提供某个中间变量的替代值，把它与 recipient 其余变量组合后，得到已知正确的 counterfactual answer。然后让 latent-CoT 模型分别在 r 和 s 上 rollout 到某个 latent step t，在这个 patch 点把 source 的某个缓存切片插入 recipient，对比 recipient 的答案是否朝 source 定义的反事实移动。

方法不是只做一次 patch，而是做一整套 intervention grid。维度包括：patch 哪个 cache segment；只换 K、只换 V、还是 K/V 一起换；是否同时复制当前 hidden state；是否使用语义相近但答案相同的 source control；是否做 decoded validation，确认被 patch 的 latent 轨迹确实对应可读出的反事实行为；以及 matched corruption，用同一区域做破坏性干预来测试 necessity。作者据此定义三个状态：active carrier，指最小且 gated 的 cache segment，在 oracle interchange 下足够，并且主要竞争解释无法匹配；carrier shift，指存在可转移效应，但活跃片段与主结论模型不同；no-call，指由于能力、支持度、decoded 行为或控制检查不过关，不能下机制判断。

从全文看，论文最重要的技术细节有三点。第一，它强调 exact source-recipient counterfactual，而不是开放式 prompt patching，这样可以避免目标答案不明确。第二，它把 sufficiency 和 necessity 分开，且 necessity 通过 matched corruption 而不是随意噪声注入来做，减少“哪里都能破坏”的伪结论。第三，它把 hidden state 与 cache object 明确区分：h_t 不是 cache 的一部分，只有显式复制时才算干预对象。这让“是当前状态在算，还是历史 value 轨迹在承载”这个问题可以被单独检验。bd:T74d,SCIT, the Suffix Cache Interchange Test, is a cache-level counterfactual intervention protocol. For a recipient problem r and a source problem s, the method first constructs an exact, verifiable counterfactual: the source supplies a changed intermediate quantity, which is then combined with the recipient’s remaining variables to define a known counterfactual answer. Both source and recipient are rolled out to a latent step t. At that patch point, a selected cache slice from the source is transplanted into the recipient, optionally together with the current hidden state, and the test checks whether the recipient moves toward the source-defined counterfactual answer.

The protocol is deliberately grid-like rather than a single patch experiment. It varies: which cache segment is patched; whether only K, only V, or both are copied; whether the hidden state is also copied; whether semantic source controls with the same answer are used; whether decoded validation confirms that the patched latent trajectory corresponds to the intended counterfactual behavior; and whether matched corruption on the same region supports necessity. Based on this battery, the paper defines three outcomes: active carrier, carrier shift, and no-call.

Three technical choices are especially important. First, the paper uses exact source-recipient counterfactuals rather than open-ended prompt patching, which keeps the target answer unambiguous. Second, it separates sufficiency from necessity, and tests necessity with matched corruption rather than arbitrary noise, reducing the risk of overcalling mechanisms. Third, it explicitly distinguishes the current hidden state from the cache object: h_t is not part of the cache unless copied by intervention. That makes it possible to ask whether the computation is carried by the present state or by a historical value trajectory.be:T6f0,The experiments are centered on controlled arithmetic settings, chosen because they allow exact counterfactual labels and clean negative controls. The main result is checkpoint-specific but strong: on the CODI-GPT2 arithmetic checkpoint, counterfactual answer transfer occurs primarily through value-cache suffix trajectories, with the strongest restricted effect in middle-to-late value segments. This region is not only sufficient under oracle interchange, but also supported by matched-corruption necessity, which is why the authors make a full mechanism call for a late-value-suffix carrier. In contrast, hidden-only transfer, key-only transfer, single-token triggers, same-answer semantic source controls, and partial-variable controls are all much weaker and do not explain the same effect.

On a Sim-CoT-style GPT-2 reproduction, the pattern is directionally similar: value-suffix sufficiency and decoded transfer are present, but matched-corruption necessity is not strong enough for a full necessity claim. The paper is explicit about that limitation.

A broader checkpoint sweep shows that the mechanism is not uniform. Some arithmetic-like GPT-2/1B cells preserve latent-tail value/KV transfer, while several competent 8B or repaired non-arithmetic cells shift the carrier to prompt-prefix or full-cache K/V. The authors call this a carrier shift rather than a replication of the CODI-GPT2 mechanism. Some cells are labeled no-call because competence gating, decoded behavior, support, or source-control checks fail. This is one of the paper’s strengths: it does not argue that latent CoT universally lives in value-cache suffixes; it provides a framework that can separate local mechanism evidence, regime shifts, and cases where no mechanism claim is justified.bf:T4bf,For a skim, focus on the protocol before the results. The introduction already states the scope clearly: the goal is not to prove a universal latent-CoT mechanism, but to define a carrier-test contract. Start with Figure 1 and the method section to understand the four-step flow: define the patch object, specify the intervention grid, validate the readout, and apply the carrier decision rule.

Then read how the arithmetic counterfactuals are constructed. That part explains why the source-recipient pairing is exact and why the protocol is not yet directly portable to open-domain reasoning tasks.

In the experiments, prioritize the CODI-GPT2 main result, because that is the only place where the paper claims a full sufficiency-plus-necessity mechanism. Then read the Sim-CoT-style checkpoint to see why it is treated as partial corroboration rather than full replication. For a deeper pass, the appendix matters: intervention tables, prompt templates, and the full evaluation battery are where the paper earns its credibility.c0:T929,方法核心是一个 iterative prune-heal-backtrack 流程。模型被表示为 residual-stream writers/readers 构成的有向图：writer 包括 token embedding、每个 attention head 的 residual contribution、每个 MLP 输出；reader 包括后续 attention/MLP 输入以及最终 logits。边表示某个 writer 对下游 reader 的信息通路。与常见直接置零不同，作者采用 clean/corrupted prompt 配对，并在关闭边时用 corrupted prompt 上对应 writer 的 counterfactual activation 替代 clean activation，避免把读入分布推离数据流形。这样“边是否必要”更接近因果替换而不是粗暴破坏。

训练上只更新一个从零开始的 LoRA adapter，底座模型冻结。初始时所有边开放。每一轮先用因果重要性估计给当前存活边排序，然后剪掉一批最弱边；接着在新边掩码下训练 LoRA，使适配后的模型尽量复现原模型输出。这里的目标不是重新学任务标签，而是通过剩余通路逼近原模型 next-token distribution，因此它更像 constrained distillation。随后用 held-out controller 决定是否接受本轮剪枝：只有当目标行为准确率仍达标，且 off-target 语言建模能力没有明显恶化时，才保留这次删除，否则回退到上一状态。这个 accept/reject 机制很重要，因为它把“更小电路”约束在“行为保真 + 通用能力保真”之内，而不是单纯追求 sparsity。

作者把最终最小可接受电路记为 C1。与 frozen search 的区别在于：传统 EAP/EAP-IG/EAP-GP 之类方法只是在固定权重上估计边重要性；这里则允许通过低秩参数更新把行为迁移到更少边上。论文还专门做了一个对照：使用同样的搜索流程但不更新权重，结果明显更差，说明收益主要来自 reshaping behavior implementation，而不是搜索器本身更聪明。

另一个技术点是 fidelity 评估不只看任务准确率，还看与原模型输出分布的 KL，以及 condensed circuit 对原模型失败模式的预测能力。也就是说，作者知道“压缩后的小电路”可能只解释修改后的网络，因此专门测试它是否仍能描述原始未修改模型。这一点让方法不只是做出一个小模型，而是尽量保留对原模型机制的解释联系。c1:T8f5,The method is an iterative prune-heal-backtrack procedure. A transformer is represented as a directed graph over residual-stream writers and readers. Writers include token embeddings, each attention head’s residual contribution, and each MLP output; readers include downstream attention/MLP inputs and final logits. Edges represent information flow from an upstream writer to a downstream reader.

A key design choice is how edges are ablated. Instead of zeroing an edge, the method uses paired clean/corrupted prompts and replaces the clean activation flowing through a closed edge with the corresponding activation from the corrupted prompt. This counterfactual replacement avoids pushing activations off-manifold, making edge necessity tests more causally meaningful than naive zero ablation.

Training updates only a freshly initialized LoRA adapter while keeping the base model frozen. Starting from all edges open, each round ranks surviving edges by causal importance, removes the weakest ones, and then trains the LoRA adapter to reproduce the original model’s outputs through the remaining graph. This is closer to constrained distillation than task finetuning: the goal is to match the original next-token distribution under a restricted internal pathway. A held-out controller then accepts the deletion only if both target-task accuracy and off-target language-modeling capability remain within tolerance; otherwise the method rolls back. The smallest accepted graph is denoted C1.

This differs sharply from frozen circuit search methods such as EAP-IG: those estimate importance under fixed weights, whereas Circuit Condensation allows low-rank adaptation to reshape where the behavior lives. The paper explicitly tests the same search loop without weight updates and finds that it loses badly, which isolates the gain to behavioral reshaping rather than better search alone.

Another strong point is the fidelity analysis. The authors do not stop at task accuracy on the adapted model. They also measure KL to the original model’s next-token distribution and test whether the condensed circuit predicts failure modes of the unmodified model better than size-matched frozen circuits. This is important because otherwise one could end up explaining only the modified network.c2:T6f6,The evaluation spans 4 behaviors, 8 models from 4 families, and 3 random seeds. Candidate edge counts range from 2,041 in GPT-2 to 43,993 in Qwen3-4B. The headline result is that in 30 of 32 settings, C1 is smaller than the strongest frozen EAP-IG baseline at comparable task accuracy, by 8.1x on average and up to 316x. The sign test gives p = 2.5e-7, with a bootstrap interval of [4.9, 13.7]. Running the same search without weight updates loses in 29 of 32 settings, supporting the claim that the benefit comes from reshaping the implementation of the behavior.

The paper then shows why smaller circuits matter operationally. The condensed circuits make exhaustive subset tests, all-pairs ablations, and edge-level necessity checks feasible. Matched frozen circuits would require a median 55x more pairwise ablations, and subset enumeration is infeasible in all 19 matched cases reported. So the size reduction changes what verification questions can actually be computed.

On fidelity, the median KL to the original model’s next-token distribution is 0.215 across the grid, and 0.056 on the IOI anchor task, compared with 0.50 for a size-matched frozen circuit. The condensed circuits also better predict where the original model will fail than frozen circuits of the same size. That is a strong indication that the method is not merely producing a compact explanation for the adapted model, but retaining explanatory contact with the original one.

The paper also discusses limits: not every behavior condenses equally well, and some appear to resist concentration under capability constraints. Those failure cases are important because they speak to whether the method is exposing genuine redundancy or simply exploiting the flexibility of LoRA to rewrite local mechanisms.c3:T4dd,For a quick read, focus on three things. First, read the introduction and the main method figure to internalize the objective: the paper is not trying to recover the one true frozen circuit, but to move a behavior into a smaller circuit under fidelity constraints. Second, read the sections defining edge gating, clean/corrupted activation replacement, LoRA-only healing, and the held-out accept/reject controller. Those choices are what make the method more than standard pruning. Third, inspect the results on circuit size, exhaustive verifiability, and fidelity to the original model.

The two questions worth probing are whether condensation is distilling an existing mechanism or creating a new local implementation, and whether condensability depends on model scale, task type, or the degree of distributed representation learned during pretraining.c4:T4be,Its value for foundation-model research is less about a new pretraining recipe and more about measurement at the pretrain/post-train boundary. Many alignment interventions—RLHF, DPO, SFT, refusal tuning, persona control, even retrieval-conditioned interaction—change how readily a model updates in multi-turn settings. If rational updating is not measured separately, training can easily turn “do not flatter the user” into “do not revise when new information arrives.” The contribution has three parts. First, it introduces a two-turn diagnostic that cleanly separates unsupported pressure from evidence-based revision. Second, it compares both training-time and inference-time interventions and shows that the trade-off is recurring rather than method-specific. Third, the mechanistic analysis suggests that the two behaviors share internal circuitry and aligned steering directions, which explains why naive suppression lacks selectivity. For anyone working on RLHF, DPO, SFT, activation steering, or agent systems that must incorporate external evidence, this is a useful warning: the intervention may be changing the model’s update threshold rather than improving truthfulness in a targeted way.c5:T906,The method has three layers. The first is the evaluation design. The authors adapt four datasets—TruthfulQA, PopQA, EX-FEVER, and AQuA—into a two-turn setup. The model first answers the question on its own. In the second turn, it receives either a pressure message that merely challenges the answer without adding information, or an evidence message that supports the correct answer. This lets the authors measure answer revision under unsupported social pressure separately from revision under informative evidence. Formally, the object of study is the transition from the first-turn answer to the second-turn answer, conditioned on the type of feedback.

The second layer is intervention comparison. They evaluate four open-weight LLMs under representative anti-sycophancy interventions spanning both training-time and inference-time control, including SFT, DPO, and activation steering. The key is that they do not rely on single-turn accuracy. Instead, they track how each intervention changes Unsupported-Yielding and Rational-Updating in the two-turn setting. They also test joint optimization settings intended to reduce sycophancy while preserving updating, and still observe a persistent trade-off.

The third layer is mechanistic analysis. The authors use gradient-based attribution patching to localize components associated with answer flips, validate them with cross-patching, and estimate contrastive steering directions for each behavior. Two findings matter most. First, the components implicated in Unsupported-Yielding and Rational-Updating overlap substantially, especially in specific layers and attention heads. Second, the steering directions for the two behaviors are positively aligned rather than cleanly separable. This implies that many interventions are not selectively suppressing sycophancy; they are perturbing a more general internal mechanism for revising answers in response to second-turn signals. Motivated by this, the paper explores a preliminary orthogonalized steering procedure: remove the component aligned with rational updating before applying anti-sycophancy steering. On TruthfulQA this yields modest and model-dependent selectivity gains, particularly at the attention-head level, but it is clearly presented as an early probe rather than a finished solution.c6:T57f,The experimental emphasis is on relative behavioral shifts rather than headline benchmark scores. Across four task families—truthfulness QA, factual QA, evidence verification, and math reasoning—the main pattern is stable: interventions that reduce Unsupported-Yielding usually also reduce Rational-Updating. This holds across DPO, SFT, and activation-steering style methods. In other words, the model becomes harder to push around by the user, but also less willing to revise when new evidence should change the answer.

The mechanistic section provides the strongest evidence. Figure 4 shows overlap in the components associated with the two behaviors. Figure 5 shows positive alignment between their steering directions. Cross-patching further supports that the localized components are not merely correlated with the behavior but causally involved in answer flips.

The orthogonalized-steering exploration reports modest selectivity gains on TruthfulQA. The paper is careful here: the gains are limited and model-dependent, so this should not be read as a mature mitigation recipe. The more important result is conceptual. It demonstrates that selective control may be possible, but only with finer representational disentanglement than simple suppression.

If you care about numbers, the most informative view is not raw final accuracy but paired changes in the two metrics under each intervention.c7:T8dc,The core idea is to combine natural-looking text with a fully controlled latent process. The teacher is Gemma-2-2B base, paired with a pretrained Gemma Scope sparse autoencoder. From the SAE latents at an intermediate layer, the authors select 8 directions that are approximately orthogonal and weakly correlated, to avoid pre-existing semantic neighborhood structure. During generation, a ring-shaped 8-state Markov chain determines which latent is active at each token. The teacher is then steered along the corresponding SAE decoder direction by adding a scaled vector into the residual stream from layers 12 through 23.

The scaling uses the latent’s average firing magnitude and layerwise residual norms. This is not just a cosmetic detail: the paper reports that injecting at a single layer lets later layers partially undo the intervention, so persistent multi-layer steering is needed to write a durable signal into the generated text. The resulting corpus still looks like ordinary language, but token probabilities are subtly biased by the current hidden state.

A small student Transformer is then trained from scratch on this corpus, with no access to the latent labels. Analysis proceeds in two stages. First, the authors test whether the student linearly encodes the posterior belief over the hidden Markov state, not merely the last state or local lexical cues. Because the latent process is known, they can compute the ground-truth belief state from the observation history and fit linear probes against it. Second, they study the geometry of the 8 latent values themselves in the student’s representation space, using class-conditioned centers, pairwise distances, and low-dimensional projections. This distinction is central: a belief state is a distribution over latent values, while concept geometry concerns how the latent values themselves are arranged.

Relative to earlier work, the novelty is threefold: the data are natural-looking rather than fully synthetic; the paper studies belief tracking and concept geometry in the same setup; and the latent directions are deliberately chosen to be unrelated, so any recovered ring geometry is more plausibly caused by the imposed dynamics than by pre-existing semantic similarity in the teacher.c8:T75c,The main empirical findings are qualitative but fairly clean. First, the student does learn belief tracking. Linear probes recover the posterior over the hidden state from internal activations, and this signal emerges progressively across layers rather than appearing only at the output. The paper also compares against simpler alternatives, such as probes based on local token information or direct state prediction, and those do not explain the results as well, suggesting the model is not merely memorizing shallow lexical patterns.

Second, the latent-state geometry is recovered. The 8 states form a ring-like arrangement in the student’s representation space, with the correct neighbor order matching the imposed Markov chain. This is important because the teacher SAE directions were selected to be approximately uncorrelated, so the ring is unlikely to be inherited from the teacher’s original semantic geometry.

Third, the control experiments matter. When the transition structure is randomized or the steering signal is weakened or removed, the ring geometry becomes much less pronounced and belief recovery degrades. The paper also compares steering strategies and finds that single-layer interventions are easier for the teacher to wash out, while multi-layer steering leaves a more learnable trace in the generated corpus.

Fourth, the authors discuss the trade-off between naturalness and learnability. If steering is too weak, the student cannot reliably infer the latent process; if it is too strong, the text distribution drifts further from ordinary language. The chosen operating point keeps the text readable while still embedding a recoverable hidden signal. The paper is more about mechanism validation than benchmark gains, so the most informative evidence is in the probe plots, geometry visualizations, and ablations rather than a single headline metric.c9:T4b5,Reported results include concrete geometric statistics:

The motivation is clear. Probes can read out information that is not actually used by the model, while SAE/CLT-style methods may surface interpretable features but still leave faithfulness and stability concerns. DAS searches for low-dimensional, causally relevant subspaces by intervening on internal states between paired examples and identifying the rotations and substitutions that best explain behavioral changes.

The experimental design is unusually important here. The authors build templated minimal pairs for three syntactic constructions across fifteen languages. Coverage is intentionally uneven where typology demands it: Chinese is excluded from number agreement because it lacks grammatical number, and German/Dutch require special handling in filler–gap templates because embedded verbs are clause-final. This matters because the paper is trying to compare mechanisms, not just outcomes, so template alignment and minimal-pair control are central to validity.

The workflow is: verify that the model behaviorally handles the construction, localize a causally implicated subspace within a source language, then transplant that intervention into the corresponding target-language position and measure whether behavior changes in the expected direction. The paper also includes controls such as random-label tests and mismatched interventions to show that the effect is not a generic perturbation artifact. A further step links transfer strength to typological similarity, leading to the claim that multilingual syntactic mechanisms are organized around typological hubs rather than arbitrary language-specific partitions.cc:T59b,The study spans 4 multilingual LMs, 15 languages, and 3 syntactic phenomena. The models differ in family, size, and training setup, which helps the authors argue that the findings are not tied to a single architecture or checkpoint. Before any interpretability analysis, they run behavioral validation to ensure the models actually exhibit the target syntactic competence on the constructed stimuli.

The main empirical findings come in three layers. First, cross-lingual mechanism transfer is consistently observed across all three constructions, not just in a few closely related language pairs. Second, transfer is graded rather than binary: stronger transfer tends to occur between typologically closer languages. Third, some languages behave like hubs, with interventions localized in those languages transferring more broadly to others. That suggests multilingual models may organize syntactic abstractions around a small number of reusable structural centers.

The controls are important. Random-label and other non-specific intervention settings substantially weaken the effect, which supports the claim that the discovered subspaces are causally tied to the target syntactic behavior rather than reflecting generic representation damage. This is not a benchmark-improvement paper, so the key numbers are intervention effect sizes, transfer success rates, and their relation to typological structure, not downstream task gains.cd:T74a,The analysis starts from the simplest binary geometry. For hidden states labeled factual vs hallucinated, define class means μ0 and μ1, and let δ = μ1 − μ0 be the mean-shift direction. The authors first test necessity: remove the component along δ and see whether classification survives. It does not; performance collapses to chance. They then test sufficiency: project onto δ alone and classify in 1D. That already recovers a large fraction of the signal, but still trails regularized logistic regression.

This motivates the second layer of analysis. In the binary case, Fisher LDA uses ΣW^-1δ rather than raw δ, so if within-class covariance is far from spherical, covariance-aware linear methods can outperform the pure mean-shift direction without invoking nonlinear structure. Since the hidden dimension is around 4,000, covariance estimation is nontrivial. The paper therefore compares raw mean-shift projection, shrinkage LDA, L2-regularized logistic regression, and a set of controlled alternatives designed to isolate mean-targeting, variance-targeting, and nonlinear effects. The result is that shrinkage LDA closes about 73% of the gap between the 1D mean-shift classifier and the full-dimensional classifier, supporting the view that most of the remaining gain is about covariance estimation under noise, not richer geometry.

LayerMix is then introduced as a practical consequence of the analysis rather than a major algorithmic invention. Since the signal is not confined to a single oracle layer but spread across a contiguous band of layers, LayerMix uses lightweight cross-validated aggregation across layers to identify and combine that informative band. The framing is intentionally modest: it is a strong, cheap baseline derived from the geometry, not a claim that multi-layer aggregation is itself the main scientific contribution.ce:T5fb,The experiments cover three 7B-scale models and three datasets under a paired-example protocol. The headline result is that removing the mean-shift direction δ drops AUROC to 0.499, essentially chance, which makes δ necessary for detection. Using only the 1D projection onto δ yields 0.834 AUROC, recovering about 78% of the above-chance performance. A practical L2-regularized logistic regression reaches 0.952 AUROC, showing that there is still useful structure beyond raw δ, but that structure remains largely linear and covariance-related.

The paper also reports Cohen’s d of roughly 1.2–1.6 along δ, even though that direction explains less than 3% of total variance. This is an important geometric point: discriminative signal can live in a very low-variance direction. In controlled comparisons against 12 alternative probe architectures, L2-LR matches or outperforms them, which supports the claim that many complex probes are mostly dealing with estimation noise rather than exploiting meaningful nonlinear structure. LayerMix reaches 0.954 AUROC without oracle-layer access and adds only about 35 seconds of overhead, suggesting that the main benefit comes from exploiting a distributed informative layer band rather than from more expressive modeling.

They compare three latent-selection methods:
- ValSel: select latents with language-distinct activation magnitudes (mean activation differences), using an l-monolinguality score.
- FreqSel: select latents that activate more frequently for a target language, with a specificity threshold T and corpus/token coverage constraints (N%, M%).
- AnnSel: trace attribution graphs with Circuit Tracer, prune to high-importance paths, then filter latents by LLM-generated annotations that explicitly mention the target language (favoring interpretability).

- Target amplification (set target latents to mean nonzero activations from target-language data).
- Distractor zero ablation (zero latents for the context language or all non-target languages).
- Distractor direction ablation (remove residual projections along distractor latent directions; one-layer vs multi-layer).
- Combined interventions (e.g., Zero+Amp, 1L+Amp).d1:T6bc,The main technical contribution is an analysis-ready perturbation framework plus a mechanistic probing pipeline. Existing adversarial summarization datasets are usually too coarse for causal tracing because they modify text at the sentence or document level. The authors instead build paired clean/corrupt summaries with explicit token-level modification maps. They define eight localized perturbation types spanning two quality axes, Readability and Adequacy, while controlling perturbation intensity through a parameter k and preserving exact token positions of edits.

Using this setup, they analyze two judge models: Themis, built on Llama-3-8B, and Prometheus, built on Mistral-7B. The experiments combine causal tracing, logit-lens vocabulary projection, and attention-head knockout. The central finding is a two-stage internal evaluation process. Lower layers, especially attention modules, are mainly involved in defect identification and signal routing. Upper-layer MLPs integrate those signals into a final rating, with the score becoming sharply encoded in the residual stream at a late layer. The paper also shows criterion-specific attention behavior: readability errors spread across nearby syntactic context, while adequacy-related perturbations stay more localized around the modified tokens.

Another useful result is the comparison with the base model. Fine-tuning does not appear to create the evaluation pipeline from scratch. The base Llama-3-8B already exhibits a routing-like substrate and late-layer score crystallization. Judge fine-tuning mainly modifies that substrate by suppressing low-layer MLP contribution at the last position and moving the crystallization point earlier by about two layers.d2:T4b2,The most important results are mechanistic. Both judges show a consistent stage split: below roughly layer 15, attention dominates error detection and routing; around layers 25 to 26, the final rating becomes sharply represented. Themis writes the score in a more concentrated top-layer step, while Prometheus distributes the write across mid-to-late layers and applies an opposite-direction correction at the final layer. The comparison to base Llama-3-8B is also notable: the base model already contains much of the routing structure, and judge fine-tuning mainly reshapes information flow rather than inventing a new circuit.

The perturbation analysis further shows that different error types induce different attention patterns. Readability defects recruit broader local context, whereas adequacy defects remain more tightly centered on the perturbed tokens. This suggests that criterion-specific supervision could be a sensible design direction for future evaluator training.

If reading selectively, the key is not every individual attack category but the connection between token-level perturbation maps, score shifts, and layer-wise decomposition of attention, MLP, and residual contributions.d3:T899,论文的技术路线分三步。

第一步是现象隔离。作者比较 released VLM 与对应 reference LLM 的文本能力差距，并引入 text-only further-training 对照，以及共享 base LLM 的 VL-versus-text matched trajectory，说明损失不是一般继续训练都会发生，而是和视觉模态适配强相关。损失最明显的不是开放式知识问答，而是那些对表面 token 格式、答案边界、最终输出规则很敏感的任务。

第二步是机制诊断。作者把问题归因到 attention-sink corruption。现代 LLM 往往会把大量注意力质量集中到少数早期位置，这些位置的 hidden state 又被少数高幅值固定特征维度主导，形成 sink。论文的假设是，这种 sink 有助于稳定每个位置对关键表面 token 的注意力分配，从而支撑格式敏感任务。VL fine-tuning 会扰动 query/key 投影 Wq、Wk；由于 logit shift 会随输入幅值放大，这种扰动在 sink 位置被特别放大，导致 per-head sink collapse。作者进一步分析不同 QK normalization 设计的差异：如果是 per-head QK-RMSNorm，可以直接去掉对原始输入幅值的显式依赖；如果只是 layerwise normalization，则每个 head 的尺度仍受整层能量分配影响，弱 head 会被进一步压缩，因此到 VL 训练开始前，某些 backbone 的 per-head sink 已经偏弱。

第三步是预测指标与干预验证。作者提出 Sink Strength，一个只在 base LLM 上通过少量 forward pass 计算的标量，用来量化 head-level sink concentration。这个指标不需要做任何 VL 训练，就能预测后续多模态适配后的文本能力损失。然后他们把 base-side sink weakness 与 post-VL gap perturbation 结合起来，区分“骨干先天脆弱”和“VL 更新额外破坏”两部分。最后做两个负对照：一是在预训练后给模型补装 QK-RMSNorm 再去做 VL 训练，发现不能复现原生架构自带的保护效果；二是对已经训练好的 VLM 做多种 weight merging，也无法把丢失的文本能力救回来。这说明问题更像训练过程中的 head-level 结构破坏，而不是事后线性修补能解决的。d4:T843,The paper proceeds in three stages.

First, it isolates the phenomenon. The authors compare released VLMs against their reference LLM backbones on a text-only evaluation suite, and add text-only further-training controls plus a matched VL-versus-text training trajectory from the same base model. This is meant to show that the degradation is not just a generic consequence of continued training, but is tied to multimodal adaptation.

Second, it proposes a mechanism: attention-sink corruption. Many modern LLMs place a large fraction of attention mass on a few early positions. Those positions are dominated by a small set of high-magnitude feature dimensions and act as sinks. The paper argues that these sinks help stabilize attention allocation in ways that matter for tasks graded on exact output form. During VL fine-tuning, perturbations to the query and key projections, Wq and Wk, induce logit shifts that scale with input magnitude. Because sink positions have unusually large magnitude, the perturbation is amplified there, causing per-head sink collapse. The architecture analysis then distinguishes per-head QK-RMSNorm from layerwise normalization: per-head normalization removes explicit raw-magnitude dependence, while layerwise normalization can still compress weak heads because each head’s scale is tied to the layer’s total energy.

Third, the paper introduces a predictive metric and tests interventions. Sink Strength is a single scalar computed on the base LLM, before VL training, to quantify head-level sink concentration. It predicts how much text capability will be lost after VL adaptation. The authors then separate base-side vulnerability from update-induced corruption by combining pre-VL sink weakness with post-VL sink-gap perturbation. Finally, they run two negative controls: injecting QK-RMSNorm after pretraining and then doing VL training, and applying several post-VL weight-merging methods. Neither recovers the protection seen in native architectures, which suggests the issue is tied to training-time head-level dynamics rather than something easily repaired afterward.d5:T64f,The study covers six released VLM–LLM pairs from families including Qwen, InternVL, and LLaVA-OneVision, with headline examples such as Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, and LLaVA-OV, plus additional controls. Several results stand out. First, the text-capability gap reaches double-digit points on multiple format-sensitive tasks, while matched text-only further training causes much smaller degradation. That supports a modality-specific effect. Second, Sink Strength is a strong predictor of post-VL damage: the headline rank correlation is Spearman rho = 0.97, and correlations remain high across six pairs and four format-sensitive tasks, with rho >= 0.88. Third, the preserved-sink versus collapsed-sink split is sharp on instruction following: every preserved-sink backbone stays within 5.4 points of its reference LLM, while every collapsed-sink backbone loses at least 7.9 points. Fifth, post-VL weight merging, including linear, spectral, and sparsified variants, fails to recover the lost text capability under the tested settings.

Overall, the experimental contribution is breadth of deployment and grounding, not tightly controlled algorithmic comparison.da:T7f3,ASIL is presented as an agent-native interaction layer rather than a single backend. The core design choice is to expose software through the deepest feasible access path available for each application. On the observation side, the agent receives a structured JSON object containing task metadata, application state, interactive elements, environment context, navigation structure, and a concise textual summary. On the action side, the agent emits a schema-constrained JSON action with explicit type, target, and parameters. The key shift is from “where to click” to “what to modify / invoke / export.”

The implementation is organized around three realization paths:
1. file-based access, where structured file formats are read and modified directly;
2. scripting-based access, where native scripting runtimes or automation APIs are used;
3. service-based access, where backend APIs or service endpoints expose semantic operations.

The paper emphasizes four design principles: completeness, semanticity, stability, and composability. Completeness addresses the partial observability of screenshots. Semanticity aligns actions with meaningful software operations. Stability avoids UI-dependent identifiers and layout drift. Composability allows complex tasks to be solved through a sequence of higher-level operations rather than long GUI event chains.

A notable systems contribution is the onboarding framework: reviewed interface profiles are compiled into validated adapter contracts. This makes ASIL more than a one-off wrapper. It resembles tool schemas or MCP-style interfaces, but with a stronger emphasis on state observability and action closure.

Importantly, ASIL is also treated as a trainable environment. The authors run small-scale SFT followed by resource- and time-limited on-policy RL. Because states and actions are structured and directly checkable, reward design and rollout efficiency become much cleaner than in screenshot-and-click settings. That is the part most relevant to agent training dynamics.db:T689,The evaluation has three layers. First, the environment and benchmark: ASIL is instantiated across 15 applications, with 300 single-application tasks and 80 multi-application tasks. The authors also render GUI snapshots from the underlying software state at every step, so ASIL and screenshot-driven agents can be compared under the same task definitions and validators. This is an important design choice because it controls for task specification while changing only the interaction interface.

Second, the interface comparison: the abstract reports that ASIL reaches above 80 with closed models on the benchmark. The paper also includes repaired GUI / 50max results, matched native-interface baselines such as LibreOffice UNO and draw.io MCP, and independent validity checks to bound the comparison. The main empirical message is not just higher end performance, but shorter and more stable trajectories. GUI agents pay a large step budget and are fragile to grounding, focus, timing, and layout errors. ASIL compresses many multi-step GUI procedures into one or a few semantic actions.

Third, the training results: the authors run small-scale SFT plus resource-limited, time-limited on-policy RL on Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-9B, and report double-digit gains. They further confirm the trend on a curated 80-task hard suite. There is also an ablation over realization patterns, comparing file, scripting, and service access routes. First, the introduction and the interface-mismatch section: this is where the paper makes its real argument, namely that many GUI-agent failures are caused by the wrong observation/action interface rather than insufficient reasoning alone. Second, read the ASIL interface definition and realization methodology carefully, especially the observation/action schema, the three access paths, and the four design principles. That tells you whether the proposal is generalizable or just engineering around a few apps. Third, inspect the benchmark construction and the comparison protocol: shared validators, GUI rendering from state, native-interface baselines, and the hard-suite training results are the places where the paper either earns or loses credibility.

A practical reading order is: problem framing → interface design → benchmark construction → training experiments. In about 30–45 minutes, that should be enough to capture the main idea. The two deeper questions worth thinking about are: how much of the gain comes from better tool interfaces versus better state representations, and whether ASIL-like environments could become a source of continual pretraining or RL curricula for software agents.dd:T792,GRAIN has three main components. First, it uses an explicit pipeline. Rather than letting the model mix extraction, graph construction, and computation inside unconstrained chain-of-thought, the task is decomposed into semantic parsing of the graph and task arguments, followed by tool execution with the appropriate graph algorithm. The motivation is straightforward: shortest path, matching, coloring, and related computations are deterministic; the real weakness of LLMs is the language-to-structure mapping.

Second, the method enforces structural invariance during training. The authors construct multiple isomorphic views of the same underlying graph: node identifiers may be random, semantic, aliased, or noisy, and the task description may range from standardized templates to more realistic narratives. The model is trained to recover the same intermediate graph despite these surface changes. This is more than ordinary augmentation, because the reward directly checks whether the predicted intermediate graph matches the ground-truth topology. That gives denser and more targeted feedback than final-answer supervision alone.

Third, GRAIN uses single-agent RL as a form of robustness distillation. The goal is not to build a multi-agent system, but to absorb into one model the robustness that would otherwise require repeated decomposition and verification across multiple agents. The RL objective jointly rewards correct structure recovery and correct tool invocation. The intended effect is to learn identifier-invariant and formulation-invariant parsing rules instead of memorizing templates.

The accompanying benchmark, GRIT, is also a substantial part of the contribution. It covers six graph problems across 31 real-world prototypes, with controlled multi-view variants for naming and narrative style. That makes it possible to separate failures of structure extraction from failures of downstream algorithmic solving.de:T6da,The experiments are built around robustness diagnosis rather than a single leaderboard number. The first result is that the robustness gap is real: under identifier shift and task-form shift, performance varies significantly even when the underlying graph is unchanged. Closed models tend to retain stronger average accuracy but still show unstable variance across naming schemes. Open models degrade much more sharply under non-canonical identifiers and realistic narratives. This is an important finding because it shows that strong performance on sanitized graph benchmarks does not imply reliable real-world graph reasoning.

Against baselines, GRAIN is reported to outperform standard CoT, SFT, and more expensive multi-agent approaches in out-of-distribution robustness while keeping latency and token cost lower. The most informative results are likely the breakdowns by naming scheme, narrative type, graph size, and task complexity. If the gains are consistent across those slices, that supports the claim that the reward is improving the language-to-structure stage rather than exploiting a narrow template.

A key ablation concerns the structural reward itself. The paper argues that rewarding intermediate graph correctness is better than rewarding only the final answer, and better than static supervision alone. The reason is intuitive: final-answer rewards are sparse and can be accidentally correct even when parsing is wrong, while structural rewards directly supervise semantic parsing quality. Although the abstract does not list all numbers, the central empirical message is that GRAIN yields more stable performance under surface perturbations and converts part of the robustness of complex multi-agent pipelines into a single model.df:T49e,A good skim has three stops. First, read the introduction and the GRIT setup carefully to understand what is actually being evaluated: not generic text-serialized graph reasoning, but robustness of language-to-graph extraction under naming and formulation shifts. Without that framing, the paper is easy to misread as just another graph benchmark. Second, read the method section with attention to the semantic parsing → tool execution pipeline and the definition of the structure invariance reward. In particular, check how the predicted graph is matched against the ground-truth topology, whether graph isomorphism is handled explicitly, and how node renaming is treated. Third, inspect the OOD splits and the ablations comparing CoT, SFT, RL, and multi-agent baselines.

If the goal is only to capture the main idea, 20–30 minutes should be enough. The deeper follow-up questions are more interesting: whether this kind of verifiable intermediate-structure RL can transfer to code dependency graphs, knowledge graph extraction, or tool-planning graphs, and whether invariance rewards could be connected to pretraining-time augmentation, canonicalization, or schema induction.e0:T465,ContextPilot expands the context-management action space and changes the RL procedure. On the tool side, it adds planning, long-term memory, and soft context offloading beyond search, deletion, and summarization. Planning gives the agent a global structure before later actions. Long-term memory stores scattered evidence in a reusable form. Soft offloading acts as adaptive compression or temporary externalization rather than hard deletion. On the training side, the paper introduces context-aware partial rollout. It identifies influential context-management actions using changes in context and policy entropy, then branches rollouts around these critical actions instead of exploring every action uniformly. For credit assignment, it estimates the advantage of an intermediate context-management action using rewards from subsequent branches. This gives a finer signal than assigning the final trajectory reward to every step. The training also uses trajectory snapshots and token-level loss masking so that edited contexts are represented without repeatedly optimizing tokens that already appeared in earlier snapshots.e1:T780,AnySearch formulates budget-aware search as a resource-constrained sequential decision problem. The state contains the interaction history h_t and remaining budget b_t. The action space has three actions: reason internally, call the search tool, or answer and terminate. Budget is charged only on external search calls, since search latency and retrieved-document tokens dominate cost relative to internal reasoning tokens.

The method uses a two-phase curriculum. Phase I is a scaffolded learning stage. The model receives explicit budget-state injection and structured reasoning prompts that encourage it to think about whether a search is necessary, how much budget remains, and how to allocate it. Budgets decay linearly during training so the policy sees a range of budget regimes instead of overfitting to a single point.

Phase II removes the scaffold entirely. Training inputs now match inference conditions: the model is given only the total budget and must autonomously manage allocation. To make this work across budgets, the paper introduces adaptive budget sampling. Rather than sampling budgets uniformly, it focuses more on budget levels where the current policy is weak, while retaining uniform smoothing for coverage. This is important because the target is not peak performance at one budget, but a stable performance curve over many budgets.

The reward is a composite objective combining answer accuracy and budget efficiency. Efficiency is measured with both absolute and relative signals. A key detail is the adaptive weighting of the efficiency term based on query difficulty, which prevents the policy from becoming overly conservative on hard questions. Without this, a strong efficiency reward would push the model toward under-searching; too weak a reward would collapse back to wasteful search. The paper’s solution is effectively a difficulty-aware trade-off controller inside RL training.e2:T660,The evaluation spans 7 benchmarks and 3 backbone models. The main result is consistent improvement over baselines across all tested budget levels, together with generalization to budget values not seen during training. That unseen-budget result is more important than a single average score, because it suggests the model learned a transferable budget-allocation behavior rather than memorizing a few discrete budget settings.

The baselines include fixed-budget RL search agents, reward-shaping methods that try to reduce redundant tool use without an explicit budget interface, and BATS-style approaches that rely on an external budget tracker. AnySearch improves not only answer quality but also tool productivity, meaning each search call yields more useful information on average. It also achieves the lowest total token consumption, which indicates the gain is not coming from replacing search with excessive internal reasoning tokens.

The ablations address three central questions. First, whether the scaffold is truly internalized: after removing explicit budget tracking and structured prompts, performance remains strong, which supports the internalization claim. Second, whether the two-phase curriculum is necessary: removing either the scaffolded phase or the scaffold-free adaptation phase hurts cross-budget robustness. Third, whether each reward component matters: removing relative efficiency, absolute efficiency, or adaptive weighting degrades the accuracy–efficiency trade-off. The paper emphasizes consistency across the full budget range and generalization to unseen budgets more than isolated peak numbers.e3:T515,A three-stage simulation pipeline:
1) Data-driven persona building: start from anonymized, aggregated behavioral signals (activity patterns, engagement, inferred demographics) and use an LLM to synthesize a structured persona profile (summaries, patterns, narrative descriptors) used as conditioning context.
2) Structured elicitation: present control/treatment variants (visual stimuli) plus a target metric (CTR/subscription) via carefully designed structured questions; each persona-conditioned agent outputs numeric scores per variant and persona-grounded rationales. Prompt format is treated as a key hyperparameter.
3) Statistical aggregation: aggregate per-persona score differences into a simulated treatment-effect distribution \(\mathcal{N}(\hat{\delta}_s, \hat{\sigma}_s)\), analogous to the normal approximation of the real experiment’s relative effect \(\mathcal{N}(\hat{\delta}_{rel}, \hat{\sigma}^2_{rel})\). Quality is mainly measured by sign agreement (improve/harm/no effect). The paper further studies persona-pool subsampling to reduce inference cost.
The main methodological distinction from prior systems is grounding personas in real behavioral signals (vs screenshot-derived synthetic personas) and systematically analyzing prompt format + persona depth/diversity + sampling.e4:T467,AgentFactory formulates an agentic system \(s\) as a pair drawn from a joint space \(\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{W}\):
- Model space \(\mathcal{M}\): includes selecting a foundation model from an available set, plus optional instruction fine-tuning choices—dataset \(\mathcal{D}\), hyperparameters \(\mathcal{H}\), and tuning method \(\phi\) (LoRA/QLoRA/full FT). For closed models, fine-tuning is disabled (empty \(d,h\)).
- Workflow space \(\mathcal{W}\): can be graphs, neural workflow representations, or executable code.
- Multi-objective evaluation: a vector of metrics \(\mathbf{g}(s_i)\) computed by evaluation functions \(\mathbf{G} = \{G_1,\dots,G_p\}\) (accuracy, cost, latency, etc.).
- Optimization: because the space is non-differentiable and partially observable, the framework uses an “LLM optimizer” to propose iterative modifications based on the history (trajectory) of candidate systems and their metric vectors.
The key delta vs prior automated workflow optimizers is explicitly incorporating model fine-tuning into the automated search loop and emphasizing multi-objective constraints.e5:T7e4,The method is an alternating optimization framework called WHALE. The joint objective is to maximize verifier reward over trajectories induced by both model parameters θ and harness h. Directly updating both at once creates a credit-assignment problem: harness search is a slow proposal-evaluate-accept loop, while online finetuning alternates rollout collection and gradient updates at a much faster cadence. WHALE avoids this mismatch by decomposing the problem into two conditional subproblems:
1) update weights with the harness fixed;
2) search for a better harness with the updated model fixed.

For the weight phase, the paper uses online RSFT. Under the current harness, the model samples multiple trajectories per prompt, keeps only verifier-accepted rollouts, and trains with supervised learning on those accepted traces. This choice is more stable than direct policy-gradient style updates and fits existing SFT pipelines well.

For the harness phase, the paper uses Meta-Harness to search over executable harness programs while keeping the model fixed. The search space includes system instructions, tool schemas, context management, parser/execution logic, and termination policy, which is much broader than prompt-only optimization.

The paper also introduces adaptive WHALE. A fixed schedule must decide how long each phase should run, but that is hard to tune: if a phase is too short, it lacks evidence; if too long, it over-optimizes against a frozen counterpart. Adaptive WHALE enforces a minimum phase length, then switches when the current phase’s training signal stops improving. This is a sensible design because the bottleneck can shift during training.

Compared with prior joint-adaptation work, the main differences are clear. Earlier methods typically co-optimize weights and textual prompts. WHALE expands the optimization target to full executable harnesses and uses conditional alternation rather than concurrent co-adaptation, prioritizing stable attribution over raw update frequency.e6:T7b3,The evaluation covers three domains: SearchQA, mathematical reasoning with code execution, and chess puzzles. Baselines include weight-only optimization, harness-only optimization, and Fast-Slow Training (FST). Importantly, their FST implementation uses the same update methods and schedule as WHALE, but restricts the search space to system/user prompts. This isolates the effect of searching over a full harness.

Main results: WHALE improves over single-component baselines by 7.67 to 24.38 percentage points, and over FST by 4.15 to 13.00 points. That suggests the gain is not just from extra tuning, but from the alternating scheme plus the richer harness search space.

A particularly useful finding is the existence of different bottleneck regimes:
- In SearchQA, harness-only search can match the peak accuracy of weight-only training with far fewer rollouts. This indicates a harness-limited regime, where retrieval and context/control logic dominate.
- In Math, harness-only search barely helps until a small weight update is applied first. After that, the same harness search becomes effective. This is a weight-limited regime, where the model’s reasoning or code-use ability must cross a threshold before harness improvements matter.

This observation explains why stagewise optimization is weak: it assumes the bottleneck stays on one side for a long stretch, while the experiments show that the bottleneck can move.

The paper also compares alternating updates against stagewise optimization directly. Under matched budgets, small alternating updates outperform stagewise by 5.32 points on SearchQA and 9.16 points on Math, and surpass the final stagewise result after using only 29% and 49% as many rollouts, respectively. That is a strong sample-efficiency result.

ATOM，Atomic Tree Operation Modeling。作者把一条 instruction-response 拆成若干原子函数单元，形式为 A=<x,f,y>，即 f(x)→y。f 是 operator，表示抽象逻辑规则或关系谓词，例如 CapitalOf、FoundedBy、Contains；x 是 operand，表示具体输入实体或数值；y 是输出结果。基于这个表示，作者可以控制两类扰动。Operand perturbation 会替换 x，并同步更新 y，使 f 仍然成立，因此逻辑关系保持有效。Operator perturbation 保持 x 不变，但修改 y，使 f(x)→y 失效，因此破坏样本的映射规则。和传统错误分类相比，ATOM 不是按语法、风格、事实类型做表面标注，而是把错误放到“是否破坏操作规则”的层面。论文还构建了 quantify error tolerance in synthetic instruction data. Existing filters tend to be either too strict, removing samples that may still teach useful behavior, or too permissive, retaining samples that corrupt the mapping the model should learn. The concrete question is not whether a sample contains an error, but which kind of error actually harms supervised fine-tuning.","importance":"The main contribution is a more structural view of data quality. The paper argues that models are much more sensitive to corrupted operators, meaning the logical relation or transformation rule in a sample, than to corrupted operands, meaning replaceable entities, names, values, or inputs. This has direct implications for synthetic-data filtering, rewriting, deduplication, and curriculum design. The practical message is to preserve valid and diverse operations first, rather than discarding samples solely because some surface operands are noisy. The evidence is strongest for SFT-style data; applying the same principle to large-scale pretraining corpora would require additional validation.","technical_approach":"The proposed framework is ATOM, short for Atomic Tree Operation Modeling. Each response is decomposed into atomic functions written as A=<x,f,y>, or f(x)→y. Here f is the operator, an abstract rule or relational predicate such as CapitalOf, FoundedBy, or Contains; x is the operand, the concrete input instance; y is the result. This representation enables controlled perturbations. Operand perturbations replace x and update y accordingly, so the operator remains valid. Operator perturbations keep x fixed but alter y, breaking the mapping defined by f. The key difference from surface-level error taxonomies is that ATOM tests whether an error preserves or destroys the functional relation being learned. The authors build an ATOM operator tree to synthesize Atomic-QA, and introduce an Atomic-X pipeline to convert existing datasets into atomic-operation form, producing Atomic-Alpaca and Atomic-MetaMath for generalization tests.","experiments":"The central result is a strong asymmetry. When operands are replaced, even by random strings, downstream performance drops by only about 2.0% relative. When operators are corrupted, performance drops by about 18.2% relative. CKA analysis shows that models trained with operand-perturbed data retain internal representations aligned with those trained on the original Atomic-QA, suggesting that they learn the operation structure rather than memorizing surface operands. The authors also construct Atomic-QA and Atomic-LIFD subsets using an operator-centered principle that preserves broad operator coverage and structural diversity. Across four model backbones and ten benchmark tasks, these datasets outperform standard instruction-data baselines including Alpaca, LIMA, WizardLM, and Magpie. Additional Atomic-X experiments on Alpaca and MetaMath support the same conclusion.","reading_guide":"Read the definition of Atomic Function, the operator tree construction, and the two perturbation mechanisms carefully; they are the core of the work. The most useful details for a data researcher are how operator coverage is measured, how reliable the atomic decomposition is, and whether operator-preserving filters can be implemented at scale. Acc(Mb,T)] / [GenTok(Mr,T) / GenTok(Mb,T)]。分子是准确率提升，单位是百分点；分母是生成 token 相对 baseline 的倍数。GenTok 只包含 reasoning tokens 和 final output tokens，不包含 input tokens。这样做是为了隔离模型自身推理行为，避免 benchmark prompt 或 evaluation harness 的输入长度差异污染指标。TES 大于 1 表示准确率提升超过 token 倍数，0 到 1 表示有收益但边际效率弱，小于等于 0 表示额外推理没有带来收益或带来负收益。这个指标和 OckBench 的 Per-Token Intelligence 不同：后者是绝对 accuracy/token，TES 是相对 baseline 的边际收益。论文还引入 Reasoning Cost Share 和 Deployment Cost Multiplier，把生成 token 行为映射到云 API 和本地部署的成本差异。一个重要设计取舍是，TES 不是通用效用函数。它默认“1 个百分点准确率提升”和“1 倍生成 token 成本”作为可比较单位，实际业务可以按 accuracy value 调整阈值。","experiments":"实验覆盖 151 个 model-benchmark runs 和 7 个 benchmark，重点比较 reasoning-enabled model 与 non-reasoning baseline 在不同任务结构上的 token 经济性。给出的主要结论是：顺序推理任务的 TES 更高，因为中间推导 token 更可能减少错误；回忆密集型任务和已接近饱和的任务 TES 较低，因为准确率提升空间小，额外 token 主要表现为冗长输出或过度思考。论文还利用 Qwen3 这类带 thinking toggle 或 reasoning effort 控制的模型族分析同一架构内增加推理努力后的边际 TES，关注“更多 thinking 是否继续有效”。部署分析部分说明，同样的 token overhead 在云 API 和自有硬件上会产生不同经济结论，因此只看生成长度或只看价格都不够。需要注意的是，TES 必须和 baseline accuracy、absolute accuracy 一起读：near-ceiling baseline 会压缩分子，near-floor baseline 可能让低绝对准确率的提升看起来较高效。","reading_guide":"建议精读三处。第一是 Section 3 的 TES 定义，重点看为什么排除 input tokens、为什么用生成 token 倍数而不是绝对 token 数、以及 TES 阈值的解释边界。第二是任务类型分层实验，重点看顺序推理、回忆密集、饱和 benchmark 之间的 TES 差异，这部分最能指导 reasoning data mixture 和 eval suite 设计。第三是 deployment analysis，重点看 Reasoning Cost Share 和 Deployment Cost Multiplier 如何把 token 行为转成部署成本。值得深挖的是负 TES 案例和同一模型族不同 reasoning effort 的边际变化，这两类结果可以反过来指导 adaptive thinking budget、router、以及 RL 阶段的长度惩罚设计。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper asks a deployment-level question that standard accuracy benchmarks do not answer: when a reasoning model emits many more tokens than an instruction-following baseline, is the accuracy gain large enough to justify the extra generation? decision，不改模型参数、不做额外训练。其原则很简单：如果某个 refusal signal 在早期步骤已经出现，并且强度足够、持续性足够，就提前把它 commit 下来，避免后续去噪过程把它冲掉。这里的关键不是强行插入拒答模板，而是利用模型自己已经给出的 refusal probability mass，只是在提交时机上做干预。\n\n为什么这样做，而不是直接调 logits 或加安全 refusal mass 更强、更稳定，且 refusal token 的 commit rate 更高。这个观察很重要，因为它把问题从“模型是否学会拒答”细化成“拒答信号能否存活到提交”。\n\n第三，RAEC 的效果。论文声称 RAEC 在 LLaDA 和 Dream 上都能降低 ASR，同时大体保持 alignment emerges and fails in diffusion language models along two separate axes: denoising step and response position. In autoregressive models, these axes are tied together, so shallow alignment is usually discussed in terms of early output tokens. In dLLMs, they are decoupled: a token can be committed early in denoising while appearing later in the final response, or a leading response position can remain unresolved until late. pre","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2608_27128.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作处理的是长上下文推理里的一个老问题：KV 的重要性定义成“唯一性”的反面：如果某个 token 的 key 在上下文其他非相邻位置存在近重复，那么删掉它后，模型仍可能通过保留下来的近重复项恢复这部分信息；如果没有重复，它更可能是不可替代的。具体做法是：对每个 token 的 key，统计有多少其他非相邻 token 与它的 key cosine similarity 超过阈值，这个 twin count 越高，说明冗余越强，重要性越低。这里有两个设计点值得注意。第一，使用 key 而不是 value 或 hidden state，是因为 eviction 决策发生在 attention 检索层面，key 更直接反映“可被匹配到的记忆地址”；第二，排除相邻 token，是为了避免把局部连续文本的平凡相似性误判成真正的语义冗余。\n\n更有意思的是它不是 standalone policy，而是 repair pass。给定任意已有 eviction 方法输出的 retained set 和 evicted set，TwinKV 检查两类错误：一类是某个被删 token 在 retained set 中没有近重复，属于 unrecoverable eviction；另一类是某个被留 token 在 retained set 内有冗余副本，属于 wasted retention。然后在不改变总预算的前提下做 swap：把前者换回，把后者换出。这样做的好处是，它不需要知道被包装方法内部如何打分，也不需要重新排序全体 token，只利用最终保留结果做局部修正。论文还专门把这种 pairwise redundancy 与 anchor-based 方法区分开：后者用单一全局参考点衡量“离群程度”，更像异常检测；TwinKV
